CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: Which of the statements given in the options is true in relation to Regulation 1.3 of the MLC 2006 which deals with seafarers qualifications?

All seafarers must hold an STCW qualification.
Only those seafarers with watchkeeping or cargo handling duties need to have any qualifications.
Young seafarers can be given full training onboard once they have joined a vessel.

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: Onboard medical care for seafarers is covered by Regulation 4.1 of the Convention. The regulation stipulates the conditions under which a medically qualified doctor must be carried onboard. Which of the given options would require such provision?
options: All vessels with over 100 persons onboard on voyages exceeding 3 days.
All passenger ships on international voyages.

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: Regulation 5.1.5 of the Convention deals with the requirements for arrangements to deal with seafarers onboard complaints. Which of the statements given in the options is true?

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: <![CDATA[Правило 5.1.5 Конвенции касается требований к механизмам рассмотрения жалоб моряков на борту. Какое из приведенных утверждений является верным?]]>
options: <![CDATA[Каждый моряк имеет право обращаться с жалобой непосредственно к капитану.]]>

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: How are existing ships affected by the accommodation requirements of the Maritime Labour Convention 2006.

There is no legislation for the accommodation requirements for existing ships.
Existing ships are subject to the accommodation requirements of the Convention only if a change of flag occurs.
CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.answer: They only need to comply with the requirements if substantial modifications, alterations or change of use has occurred.

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: <![CDATA[Каким образом требования к жилым помещениям, предусмотренные в Конвенции 2006 года о труде в морском судоходстве, затрагивают существующие суда?]]>

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: <![CDATA[Какой из предложенных вариантов является требованием согласно правилу 2.1 Конвенции, которое касается трудовых договоров с моряками?]]>

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: There are certain conditions regarding the suitability of a person to serve as a ship’s cook and the Master must provide evidence that the requirements are being met. Select from the options the one which is correct?

<![CDATA[Лицу, назначенному судовым поваром, должен быть не менее 21 года.]]>
<![CDATA[Лицу, назначенному судовым поваром, должен быть не менее 16 лет.]]>

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: <![CDATA[关于人员是否可以充当船只厨师有一些条件，船长必须提供证据表明符合这些要求。请选择一个正确选项。]]>

<![CDATA[指定为船只厨师的人员必须至少为 21 岁。]]>
<![CDATA[指定为船只厨师的人员必须至少为 16 岁。]]>

options: To monitor and enforce compliance.
To adapt and implement national legislation.

To generate policies and procedures to ensure onboard compliance.

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: <![CDATA[В соответствии с требованиями КТМС-2006, какова главная роль компетентного органа или назначенной им признанной организации?]]>

<![CDATA[Обеспечение соблюдения требований каждым государством членом.]]>
<![CDATA[Выработка политик и процедур для обеспечения соблюдения требований на борту судна.]]>

<![CDATA[确保每个成员国的合规性。]]>

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: Once the MLC 2006 enters into force, which of the given options will have the practical responsibility for maintaining ongoing compliance onboard a vessel?
options: Ship’s Master and Senior Officers.
Flag State authorities.
Port State authorities.
Shipowner/operator.

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: <![CDATA[Кто из упомянутых ниже лиц будет нести практическую ответственность за поддержание постоянного соблюдения требований на борту судна после вступления в силу КТМС-2006?]]>
options: <![CDATA[Капитан судна и старшие офицеры.]]>

<![CDATA[Органы государства порта.]]>
<![CDATA[Судовладелец / судоходная компания.]]>

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: <![CDATA[一旦 MLC 2006 生效，以下哪个选项将对保持船上持续合规性负有实际责任？]]>

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: Which of the statements given in the options is true in relation to the hours of work for seafarers under the MLC 2006, Regulation 2.3?
options: No seafarer should normally work more than 72 hours in any 7 day period.
No seafarer should ever work more than 72 hours in any 7 day period .
The hours of work requirement is fully met if a seafarer never works more than 14 hours in a 24 hour period.
After working for 14 hours a seafarer must be given a minimum of 6 hours rest.
CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.answer: No seafarer should normally work more than 72 hours in any 7 day period.

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: <![CDATA[Какое из утверждений является верным в отношении продолжительности рабочего времени для моряков по правилу 2.3 КТМС-2006?]]>
options: <![CDATA[В обычных обстоятельствах ни один моряк не должен работать больше 72 часов в течение 7-дневного периода.]]>
<![CDATA[Моряк никогда не должен работать больше 72 часов в течение 7-дневного периода.]]>

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: The arrangements for payment of seafarers’ wages are dealt with under Regulation 2.2 of the Convention. What arrangements, if any, are required regarding allotments under this regulation?

Seafarers can only allot their full wage each month.
Shipowners may charge seafarers up to 10% of their wages to cover the cost of allotment arrangements.

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: <![CDATA[海员工资支付安排由公约规则 2.2 规定。根据此规则的规定，工资分配（如果有的话）需要有什么安排？]]>

The International Shipping Federation.
CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.answer: The International Labour Organisation.

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: <![CDATA[Чтобы обеспечить справедливость и последовательность проверок, проводимых государством порта в соответствии с КТМС-2006, предусмотрен набор рекомендаций, которым должны следовать инспекторы. Какая организация приняла и одобрила эти рекомендации?]]>
options: <![CDATA[Международная организация труда.]]>
<![CDATA[Международная морская организация.]]>
<![CDATA[Международная ассоциация классификационных обществ.]]>
<![CDATA[Международная федерация судоходства.]]>
CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.answer: <![CDATA[Международная организация труда.]]>

CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.question: <![CDATA[为了确保 MLC 2006 港口国检查公平一致，检查员应遵循一些指南。哪个组织采纳并批准了这些指南？]]>
options: <![CDATA[国际劳工组织。]]>
<![CDATA[国际海事组织。]]>
<![CDATA[国际船级社协会。]]>
<![CDATA[国际航运联合会.]]>
CD0192 — MLC 2006 Onboard Responsibiliti.answer: <![CDATA[国际劳工组织。]]>

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: The MLC 2006 requires that Shipowners ensure that certain arrangements are in place for the payment of seafarers’ wages. Which one of the given options is a mandatory requirement of the regulation dealing with payment of wages?
options: Each seafarer must be issued with an account of wages due, on a regular basis, onboard the ship.
Wages must be paid weekly.
Arrangements must be in place to allow seafarers to allot up to a maximum of 10% of their wages each month.
An account of all wages paid during employment onboard must be sent to the seafarer’s home after they have left the vessel.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Each seafarer must be issued with an account of wages due, on a regular basis, onboard the ship.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: A renewal inspection of a ship is to be carried out prior to the expiry of the vessels existing Maritime Labour Certificate. If the inspection is carried out 2 months before expiry of the original certificate when will the new certificate expire?
options: On the fifth anniversary of the expiry date of the original certificate.
On the fifth anniversary of the date of the renewal inspection.
On the fifth anniversary of the date that the previous intermediate survey was carried out.
On the date that the Declaration of Maritime labour Compliance expires.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: On the fifth anniversary of the expiry date of the original certificate.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: When considering the role of the port State control authorities in relation to the Maritime Labour Convention, 2006, which one of the statements given in the options is true?
options: PSC is responsible for inspecting all foreign vessels trading from a port under its jurisdiction.
PSC is responsible for inspecting all vessels trading from a port under its jurisdiction.
PSC is only responsible for inspecting foreign vessels flying the flag of any ratifying Member State trading from a port under its jurisdiction.
PSC is only responsible for inspecting foreign vessels flying the flag of a non-ratifying Member State trading from a port under its jurisdiction.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: PSC is responsible for inspecting all foreign vessels trading from a port under its jurisdiction.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: When drawing up the policies addressing the requirements of the MLC, 2006, regulation dealing with medical care which of the given options should be included by the Shipowner.
options: The arrangements for provision of medical and dental care in port.
Details of the cost to the seafarer of medical care onboard and ashore when in port.
The maximum number of treatments that a seafarer is entitled to whilst employed aboard ship.
Details of the medical conditions which are excluded from a seafarer’s entitlement to medical care whilst in employment.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The arrangements for provision of medical and dental care in port.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Which of the following statements is true when considering MLC, 2006, compliance?
options: All of the requirements of MLC, 2006 must be complied with.
Only the 14 areas identified for inspection and certification requirements need to be complied with.
Port State control and flag State inspections are restricted to the 14 areas identified for inspection and certification.
Ships flying the flag of non-ratifying states do not need to comply with any of the requirements of MLC, 2006.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: All of the requirements of MLC, 2006 must be complied with.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: What are the age requirements for seafarers undertaking regular night work onboard ship according to Regulation 1.1 of the MLC, 2006?
options: Seafarers must be at least 18 years old.
Seafarers must be at least 16 years old.
Seafarers must be at least 21 years old.
There is no minimum age as long as seafarers are qualified for the work.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Seafarers must be at least 18 years old.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: The manning levels required onboard ship are covered by Regulation 2.7 of the MLC, 2006. Which one of the options identifies the manning level specified in this regulation?
options: Sufficient personnel for safe, efficient secure operation.
The number of personnel stated on the Safe Manning Certificate.
Sufficient personnel to ensure two persons on a bridge watch at sea.
Sufficient personnel so that no overtime work is required.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Sufficient personnel for safe, efficient secure operation.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: What s the maximum period of validity of a Maritime Labour Certificate issued under MLC, 2006?
options: 5 years.
2 years.
3 years.
6 months.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: 5 years.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Which of the given statements is the most accurate in relation to an Interim Maritime Labour Certificate, IMLC, issued as part of the MLC, 2006 certification requirements?
options: An IMLC has a validity of 6 months maximum.
An IMLC can be renewed when it expires if a Shipowner has applied for a Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance for a vessel.
An IMLC is issued to a vessel if the vessel fails to meet the initial inspection requirements.
An IMLC can only be issued to a newly delivered ship.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: An IMLC has a validity of 6 months maximum.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: It is a requirement of MLC, 2006 that either hours of work or hours of rest must be regulated. Where hours of rest are regulated a minimum rest of 10 hours in any 24 hours must be allocated which may be split into a maximum of two periods no more than 14 hours apart. What is the minimum duration for at least one of the rest periods?
options: 6 hours.
8 hours.
5 hours.
7 hours.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: 6 hours.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: With regard to qualifications and training covered by Regulation 1.3 of the Maritime Labour Convention, 2006, which of the options is accurate.
options: All seafarers’ must be appropriately qualified or trained to carry out their duties onboard ship.
Only STCW approved qualifications and training is recognised under MLC, 2006.
Only seafarers identified on the Safe Manning Certificate need to be qualified or trained.
Seafarers under the age of 18 years do not require any previous training or qualifications to work onboard a ship as they are only considered as trainees.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: All seafarers’ must be appropriately qualified or trained to carry out their duties onboard ship.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Where existing policies and procedures exist primarily for other purposes but which also meet the requirements of part of the MLC, 2006 what action is required by the Shipowner with respect to their responsibilities under the Convention?
options: Identify the evidence sources in part 2 of the DMLC.
Rewrite the policies and procedures specifically for MLC, 2006.
Duplicate the evidence records so that there is a separate record specifically for MLC, 2006.
Rename the policies and procedures to reflect the role they have in meeting MLC, 2006 compliance.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Identify the evidence sources in part 2 of the DMLC.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: The MLC, 2006 regulation dealing with the minimum age of seafarers also includes other requirements relating to young seafarers. Which one of the given options will the Shipowner need to have in place to meet these requirements?
options: A policy identifying suitable or restricted work activities for young seafarers.
A policy prohibiting young seafarers from working at night under any circumstances.
A policy prohibiting training activities for young seafarers at night.
A policy which allows young seafarers to work at any time under supervision.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: A policy identifying suitable or restricted work activities for young seafarers.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Seafarers’ employment agreements are covered by Regulation 2.1 of MLC, 2006. Which of the given options is a requirement of this regulation?
options: All seafarers must be issued with a copy of their employment agreement.
Seafarers only need to be issued with a copy of their agreement if they request it.
Seafarers do not need to be issued with an employment agreement if it is based on a collective bargaining agreement.
As long as a specimen of the seafarers’ employment agreement is displayed onboard the ship there is no need to issue copies to individual seafarers.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: All seafarers must be issued with a copy of their employment agreement.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Ships’ accommodation requirements under MLC, 2006 are detailed in Regulation 3.1 of the Convention. Which of the statements given in the options is the most accurate in respect of application of these requirements?
options: The full accommodation requirements apply to all ships of ratifying Member States constructed after the Convention enters into force unless specifically exempted.
The full accommodation requirements apply to all ships once the Convention enters into force.
The full accommodation requirements apply to all ships flying flags of ratifying Member States.
The full accommodation requirements apply to all ships over 3000 gross tonnage regardless of the flag they fly.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The full accommodation requirements apply to all ships of ratifying Member States constructed after the Convention enters into force unless specifically exempted.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Complete the following statement from the options given. In meeting the requirements of the MLC, 2006, relating to medical certification of seafarers, the Shipowner...
options: ...must include arrangements for revalidating medical certificates which may expire during a voyage.
...need only have checks in place to ensure each seafarer’s medical certification is valid at the start of their employment.
...should accept medical certificates issued by any medical practitioner.
...can only accept medical certificates issued by an approved medical practitioner from the seafarer’s own country.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: ...must include arrangements for revalidating medical certificates which may expire during a voyage.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: A Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance is in two main parts. Who is responsible for completing part 1 of the declaration?
options: The Competent Authority.
The Shipowner.
The International Labour Organisation.
A port State control officer.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The Competent Authority.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Where would details of exemptions granted by a competent authority, under MLC, 2006, be recorded?
options: In part 1 of the Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance.
On a vessels Maritime Labour Certificate.
In the ships official log book.
On the Safe Manning Certificate.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: In part 1 of the Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: How many main parts are there in a Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance?

The appointed competent authority will normally complete part 1 of the Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance on behalf of a Member State. Which of the given options is the most accurate with regard to part 1 of the declarations issued by an individual Member State?
options: There may be some variations in the details within the document to reflect any exemptions granted to a shipowner for a particular ship by the Member State.
All of the DMLCs issued to all shipowners will be identical apart from the vessel’s name, number and tonnage as they only contain details of the national laws and regulations of that Member State.
Every part 1 of a DMLC issued by a Member State will be different as it must be written to accommodate the measures entered into part 2 by the Shipowner.
All of the DMLCs issued to an individual Shipowner by a particular Member State will be identical.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: There may be some variations in the details within the document to reflect any exemptions granted to a shipowner for a particular ship by the Member State.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: In addition to a signed copy of their employment agreement each seafarer is also entitled to be provided with other documentation under the requirements of the MLC, 2006. Which one of the given options should a seafarer also expect to receive?
options: Documented record of his work onboard ship.
An invoice detailing the charges for medical care provided onboard ship.
An invoice covering the cost of food provided during employment onboard ship.
A letter to hand to the Master of the seafarer’s next ship detailing any complaints the seafarer had raised during the current employment.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Documented record of his work onboard ship.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Which of the statements given in the options is the most accurate with respect to recreational facilities specified in the MLC, 2006?
options: The mandatory part of the Code only requires that appropriate recreational facilities should be provided onboard by the Shipowner.
Specific details of the type and range of recreational facilities which must be provided onboard ship are given in the mandatory part A Code.
There is no requirement for the Shipowner to provide seafarers’ recreational facilities onboard a ship.
Shipowners must ensure that all of the recreational facilities detailed in part B of the Code are provided onboard their ships.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The mandatory part of the Code only requires that appropriate recreational facilities should be provided onboard by the Shipowner.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: An Interim Maritime Labour Certificate can only be issued under certain circumstances and if certain conditions are met. Which of the given options is one of the conditions of issue of an IMLC?
options: The vessel’s Master must be familiar with the requirements of MLC, 2006.
The vessel must hold a valid DMLC.
The vessel must have previously held an Interim Maritime Labour Certificate.
The Shipowner must state their intention to draw up suitable policies and procedures to ensure compliance.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The vessel’s Master must be familiar with the requirements of MLC, 2006.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: The reference periods used in the regulation relating to hours of work and hours of rest are 24 hours and 7 days. How is the period of 24 hours apparently being interpreted by the majority of flag States?
options: Any consecutive period of 24 hours.
Midnight to midnight.
Noon to noon.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Any consecutive period of 24 hours.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Which of the statements given in the options best describes the Maritime Labour Convention, 2006?
options: It is the result of a review and consolidation of existing labour standards.
It is a completely new set of labour standards.
It is a collection of existing labour standards.
It is a new revision of STCW 95.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: It is the result of a review and consolidation of existing labour standards.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Which of the given options is the gross tonnage limit for which certification is a mandatory requirement under MLC, 2006?
options: Vessels over 500 gross tonnage.
Vessels over 200 gross tonnage.
Vessels over 3000 gross tonnage.
Vessels over 5000 gross tonnage.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Vessels over 500 gross tonnage.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Shipowners often use placement and recruitment services to supply crews for their vessels. What requirement does the MLC, 2006 have in relation to such services which are based in a ratifying Member State?
options: The service must be licensed or certified.
The service can only provide seafarers who are nationals of that Member State.
Shipowners can only employ seafarers supplied by such a service.
Only public services are allowed to operate in a ratifying Member State.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The service must be licensed or certified.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Complete the following statement by selecting the most accurate of the given options. Shipowners can expect that each Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance issued to them by...
options: ... an individual Member State will be very similar.
... an individual Member State will be totally different.
... an individual Member State will be identical.
...all Member States will be identical.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: ... an individual Member State will be very similar.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: MLC, 2006 requires that each vessel has an onboard complaints procedure. Which of the given statements is accurate with regard to these requirements?
options: Seafarers should have the right to complain directly to the ship’s Master if they wish.
Complaints must be presented to the ship’s Master by an appointed representative of the seafarers.
Seafarers must only take their complaints to their immediate superior who will refer them to a higher level if they feel it appropriate.
Seafarers must address their complaints directly to the ship’s Master at all times.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Seafarers should have the right to complain directly to the ship’s Master if they wish.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: With reference to the requirements for recreational facilities onboard ship under the MLC, 2006, which of the following statements is the most accurate?
options: Shipowners must have programmes to maintain and continuously improve the recreational facilities onboard ship.
The Shipowner must provide recreational facilities onboard ship but the crew must cover the cost of maintenance and improvement.
The Shipowner has no duty to provide any recreational facilities under the requirements of the Convention.
Seafarer’s welfare organisations are responsible for providing and maintaining recreational facilities onboard ship.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Shipowners must have programmes to maintain and continuously improve the recreational facilities onboard ship.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Which of the given options best describes one of the main aims of the Maritime Labour Convention, 2006?
options: It will ensure a level playing field for the Shipowner.
It will increase the number of seafarers working onboard ships.
It will reduce the number of inspections carried out onboard ships.
It will increase the number of complaints from seafarers.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: It will ensure a level playing field for the Shipowner.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: In order to meet the MLC, 2006, requirements covering food and catering certain evidence of compliance must be provided to inspectors. Which of the given statements is the most accurate in relation to Shipowners requirements for the documented evidence that should be maintained onboard their ships?
options: The documents maintained onboard should include reference to menu planning and nutritional quality of the meals.
Only a record of inspections of the provision stores and catering facilities will be required.
A record of the checks carried out to verify the age and qualifications of the cook will be sufficient evidence in the majority of cases.
If the galley is clean and none of the crew has had any complaints about the food there is no need to maintain documented evidence.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The documents maintained onboard should include reference to menu planning and nutritional quality of the meals.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: The MLC, 2006, requires that seafarers are paid regularly for the services. What is the recommended maximum interval for the payments to be made?
options: Monthly.
Weekly.
At the end of each voyage.
Every 3 months.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Monthly.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Which date is considered as the construction date of a new vessel according to MLC, 2006?
options: The date the keel is laid.
The date the vessel enters into service.
The date the vessel is launched.
The date the order is placed for the vessel.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The date the keel is laid.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Complete the following statement with regard to the requirements for onboard medical care under the MLC, 2006. To meet the requirements of the Convention regulation dealing with medical care...
options: ...all ships carrying more than 100 persons on international voyages of more than 3 days must carry a qualified medical doctor.
...all ships carrying passengers must carry a qualified medical doctor.
...all ships with more than 10 crewmembers onboard must carry a fully qualified doctor.
...all ships carrying more than 100 persons must carry a qualified medical doctor.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: ...all ships carrying more than 100 persons on international voyages of more than 3 days must carry a qualified medical doctor.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Which element of the Maritime Labour Convention, 2006, is considered as guidance rather than being mandatory?
options: Part B of the Code.
Part A of the Code.
The regulations.
The articles
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Part B of the Code.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Who has the responsibility for drawing up suitable policies and procedures to ensure that the requirements of the national laws of the flag State and therefore the requirements of the Maritime Labour Convention, 2006, are being met?
options: The Shipowner.
The Member State.
The Competent Authority.
A Recognized Organisation.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The Shipowner.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: The requirements for persons responsible for cooking and food preparation onboard ships are detailed in the Convention under the regulation dealing with food and catering. Which of the given statements best describes the requirement?
options: The person must be properly trained and qualified.
The person responsible for cooking must always be a qualified ships cook.
The person responsible for cooking must hold an STCW cook’s qualification.
The person responsible for cooking is not required to be trained or qualified at all if there are less than ten crewmembers onboard ship.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The person must be properly trained and qualified.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: When determining the level of manning onboard ship the Shipowner must obviously refer to the minimum levels shown on the vessels safe manning certificate or document. What other factor does the MLC, 2006, require be taken into account in relation to manning levels?
options: The fatigue risk due to operational requirements.
The overall cost of crewing the vessel.
The availability of suitable seafarers.
How many ships the Shipowner operates and the number of seafarers employed.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The fatigue risk due to operational requirements.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Where would a record of all MLC, 2006, inspections be found?
options: On or appended to the vessel’s DMLC.
On or appended to the vessel’s Maritime Labour Certificate.
In the vessels official log book.
On the vessels certificate of registry.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: On or appended to the vessel’s DMLC.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: If, during an MLC, 2006, renewal inspection, carried out two months before the expiry date of the certificate, a number of deficiencies and non-conformances are found but the Shipowner cannot agree a rectification action plan with the inspector, what are the likely consequences?
options: The inspector would refuse to renew the Maritime Labour Certificate and may withdraw the existing certificate.
The inspector would issue an Interim Maritime Labour Certificate until a plan could be agreed.
The vessel would be allowed to sail and keep the existing certificate as it had not expired.
The vessel would be immediately removed from the registry.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The inspector would refuse to renew the Maritime Labour Certificate and may withdraw the existing certificate.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Which of the given options would be a reasonable example of non-compliance in relation to the requirements of MLC, 2006?
options: An invalid Maritime Labour Certificate.
Record of accommodation inspections incomplete.
A faulty light fitting in the ship’s galley.
A lack of books in the ship’s library.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: An invalid Maritime Labour Certificate.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: What would a Shipowner expect the consequences of a serious deficiency being uncovered during an MLC, 2006, inspection where the deficiency was not considered to present a health or safety risk?
options: The vessel would be allowed to sail once a rectification action plan had been agreed.
The vessel would be detained until the deficiency was rectified.
The Maritime Labour Certificate would be withdrawn.
There would be no action taken as there was no health or safety risk associated with the deficiency.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The vessel would be allowed to sail once a rectification action plan had been agreed.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Which of the following statements is true in relation to a Declaration of Maritime labour Compliance issued under the MLC, 2006?
options: A Shipowner will be issued with a separate DMLC for each vessel that they operate which is covered by the Convention.
A Shipowner will be issued with a single DMLC to cover all of the vessels registered with a particular Member State.
A Shipowner will be issued with a single DMLC to cover all the vessels they operate which are covered by the Convention.
A Shipowner will only require a DMLC for vessels over 3000 gross tonnage.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: A Shipowner will be issued with a separate DMLC for each vessel that they operate which is covered by the Convention.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Where would a Shipowner find details of any ship specific requirements that a competent authority may have under the MLC, 2006?
options: In part 1 of the Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance.
In part 2 of the Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance.
On the Maritime Labour Certificate issued to a vessel.
On the vessels certificate of registry document.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: In part 1 of the Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: The ILO guidelines for flag State and port State inspections under MLC, 2006, detail the actions that inspectors may and must take in the event of deficiencies, non-conformances and non-compliance being found onboard. Where would a Shipowner find details of any additional penalties or fines that may be applied in such circumstances?
options: Contained in the national laws of the Member State.
In the text of the Maritime Labour Convention, 2006.
On the vessels Maritime Labour Certificate.
In the appendices of the Maritime Labour Convention, 2006.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Contained in the national laws of the Member State.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: What is the likely consequence for a vessel which has an invalid Maritime labour Certificate that is boarded by a port State control officer in a foreign port?
options: The vessel will be subject to a full detailed inspection.
The port State control officer will carry out a renewal inspection in order to issue a new certificate.
The vessel will be detained indefinitely.
The vessel will not be allowed to complete cargo operations in that port.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The vessel will be subject to a full detailed inspection.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: When did the Maritime Labour Convention, 2006 enter into force?
options: 12 months after the ratification criteria were met.
6 months after the ratification criteria were met.
24 months after the ratification criteria were met.
Immediately after the ratification criteria were met.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: 12 months after the ratification criteria were met.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Which one of the given options identifies the main ratification criteria for entry into force of the MLC, 2006?
options: 33% world tonnage and 30 Member States.
25% world tonnage and 30 Member States.
33% world tonnage and 20 Member States.
25% world tonnage and 20 Member States.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: 33% world tonnage and 30 Member States.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: Which one of the given options is often used to describe the MLC, 2006 in terms of the maritime regulatory framework?
options: The Fourth Pillar.
The Fourth Layer.
The Fourth Convention.
The Fourth Column.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: The Fourth Pillar.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: What details would be expected to be entered into part 1 of a Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance?
options: Details of the national laws and regulations of the Member State relating to the requirements of the MLC, 2006.
Details of the Shipowners policies and procedures which will meet the requirements of the national laws and regulations of the flag State.
Part 1 of the DMLC only contains details of the vessel it has been issued to showing the exemptions that have been granted to that vessel.
The articles, regulations and part A of the Code of the Convention.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Details of the national laws and regulations of the Member State relating to the requirements of the MLC, 2006.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: The Maritime Labour Convention, 2006, details the requirement to have a formal procedure to deal with onboard complaints by seafarers. Which of the statements given in the options is a key element of this requirement?
options: Complaints should be dealt with at the lowest level where possible.
The Master must be directly involved in hearing all complaints made onboard ship.
The procedure should only cover complaints relating to health and safety matters.
Complaints relating to food and catering are excluded as they will generally be based on personal preferences.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: Complaints should be dealt with at the lowest level where possible.

CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.question: As well as vessels registered with a ratifying Member State which are constructed after the Convention enters into force, which one of the given options will also be required to conform to the accommodation requirements detailed in the regulations?
options: An existing vessels, registered with a ratifying Member State, undergoing extensive modifications to the accommodation.
Any vessel, registered with a ratifying Member State, at the time of its renewal survey.
Any vessel changing its registration to a ratifying Member State.
All vessels, ten years after entry into force of the convention.
CD0193 — MLC 2006 Shipowner's Responsibi.answer: An existing vessels, registered with a ratifying Member State, undergoing extensive modifications to the accommodation.

CD0197 — MLC 2006, Basic Introduction.question: Qual das afirmações a seguir é verdadeira de acordo com o regulamento da MLC 2006 que trata do atendimento médico dos marinheiros?

CD0197 — MLC 2006, Basic Introduction.question: Quando as autoridades de controle do estado do porto realizam inspeções do navio de acordo com os requisitos da MLC 2006, ela deve ser feita de acordo com a cláusula "tratamento não mais favorável". options: Navios que navegam sob a bandeira de um estado não ratificador.
Navios que navegam sob a bandeira do estado membro que visitam um porto.
Navios de bandeira estrangeira que navegam sob a bandeira de um estado membro ratificador.
Navios construídos ou entregues antes da data de entrada em vigor da convenção.
CD0197 — MLC 2006, Basic Introduction.answer: Navios que navegam sob a bandeira de um estado não ratificador.

CD0197 — MLC 2006, Basic Introduction.question: When Port State Control Officers carry out ship inspections according to the requirements of the MLC 2006 they must do so with the regard to the ‘no more favourable treatment’ clause. Ships built or delivered before the entry into force date of the Convention.

CD0197 — MLC 2006, Basic Introduction.question: 根据 MLC 2006 的要求，港口国监督官员执行船舶检查时，必须遵循“不存在更优惠待遇”条目。该条目要防止哪些船舶受到更优惠待遇？

CD0197 — MLC 2006, Basic Introduction.answer: <![CDATA[Le navi battenti bandiera di uno Stato che non ha ratificato la convenzione. ]]>

CD0213 — Passage planning with ECDIS.question: The illustration shows a vessel on passage with ARPA radar target information over laid on ECDIS, and vector length is 12 minutes. Is there any risk of collision with the target?
