CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which of the following best describes what we mean by ‘power factor’ in an AC electrical system?
options: It is the proportion of apparent power which is delivered as active power
It is the ratio of power drawn from the generator to its maximum capacity
It is ratio of reactive power to active power
It is the proportion of apparent power which is converted to reactive power
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: It is the proportion of apparent power which is delivered as active power

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: The battery in the circuit shown has an output of 6 Volts. The resistance of the upper resistor is 3 Ohms and the lower resistor is 9 Ohms. What voltage is dropped across the upper resistor according to Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law?
options: 1.5 Volts
2 Volts
1 Volt
It cannot be calculated from the information given
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: 1.5 Volts

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: The battery in the circuit shown has an output of 1.5 Volts. The resistors are 32.75 Ohms each. What voltage is dropped across the right hand resistor?
options: 1.5 Volts
0.05 Volts
0.75 Volts
It cannot be calculated from the information given
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: 1.5 Volts

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which of the following best describes how the apparent power of an AC electrical circuit with a single coil as a load can be calculated?
options: P = V.I
P = I².R
P = I².X
P = V.I Cos Φ
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: P = V.I

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which of the following best describes how a capacitor works?
options: It stores energy like a fast charging battery
It converts electricity to magnetism
It converts electricity to heat
It converts electricity to higher voltages
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: It stores energy like a fast charging battery

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which of the following best describes why traditionally ships’ electrical systems have operated with an insulated neutral?
options: So as to minimise the risk of essential equipment tripping
So as to minimise the risk of generator damage
So as to minimise the cost of the electrical network
So as to minimise the risk of electrocution
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: So as to minimise the risk of essential equipment tripping

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which of the following best describes one reason why people receiving electric shocks from high voltage (HV) systems are more likely to die than those receiving shocks from low voltage (LV) systems?
options: The safe exposure time to current falls rapidly as the voltage increases
They are likely to fall further from HV equipment
They are less well trained than people working on LV
They are more likely to have sweaty hands than people working on LV
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: The safe exposure time to current falls rapidly as the voltage increases

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which one of the following best describes reactive power in an AC electrical circuit?
options: Reactive power is easily converted back to electricity
Reactive power reacts against the force of gravity
Reactive power reacts against the rotation of a rotor
The more reactive power in a circuit the more efficient it is
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: Reactive power is easily converted back to electricity

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: An AC circuit delivers an active power of 30 kW when supplied at 400 Volts and 125 Amps. Which of the following is the reactive power?
options: 40 kVAr
4 kVAr
30 kW
It cannot be calculated from the information given
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: 40 kVAr

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which one of the following best describes why arc and blast are more of a problem with high voltage (HV) electrical systems?
options: The amount of energy available in a HV circuit tends to be much higher
Arcs cannot form in air at less than 800 Volts
Blasts only happen when faults occur in a confined space like an HV cabinet
HV circuit breakers are big and slow to operate
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: The amount of energy available in a HV circuit tends to be much higher

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which of the following is the level at which electricity becomes high voltage, according to the International Electro-technical Commission standard for ships?
options: AC electricity above 1,000 Volts
AC electricity above 11,000 Volts
DC electricity above 1,000 Volts
AC electricity above 50,000 Volts
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: AC electricity above 1,000 Volts

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: The battery in the circuit shown has an output of 24 Volts. If the resistance of the upper resistor is 3 Ohms and the lower resistor is 5 Ohms what current should be flowing in the circuit?
options: 3 Amps
4 Amps
6 Amperes
It cannot be calculated from the information given
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: 3 Amps

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: The battery in the circuit shown has an output of 12 Volts. If the resistance of the upper resistor is 3 Ohms what current should be flowing in the circuit?
options: It cannot be calculated from the information given
4 Amperes
4 Amps
36 Amps
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: It cannot be calculated from the information given

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which of the following best describes one of the ways that might cause an electrical conductor to suffer voltage overload?
options: Accidental connection to the wrong supply
Insulation too thin
Fuse failure
An earth fault
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: Accidental connection to the wrong supply

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Sometimes it is possible to see electrical conductors, such as busbars, which have no insulation covering parts of them. Which one of the following best describes why these uninsulated live parts do not normally cause a short circuit?
options: The surrounding air has been used as the insulation
Insulation is fitted but it is so thin that it is not noticeable
High speed overload trips are fitted to disconnect the supply
Each conductor is surrounded by a magnetic field which contains the electricity
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: The surrounding air has been used as the insulation

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: In analysing AC electrical circuits it is common practice to use impedances. Which one of the following best describes what an ‘impedance’ is?
options: It expresses the practical effect of resistance, capacitance and inductance for a single or group of components
It expresses the practical effect of inductance for a single or group of components
It expresses the practical effect of reactance in a circuit
It expresses the theoretical effect of reactance in a circuit
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: It expresses the practical effect of resistance, capacitance and inductance for a single or group of components

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: A man accidently receives an electric shock resulting in a current of 2 mA flowing through his hands and chest. Which of the following best describes the likely effect on him?
options: He will feel tingling or mild pain
He will feel nothing
He will feel severe pain from burns
He will be killed
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: He will feel tingling or mild pain

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which one of the following best describes the meaning of ‘voltage stress’ when applied to ships’ electrical cables?
options: It is the voltage per millimetre of insulation
It is the voltage drop per metre of cable length
It is the voltage drop caused by a right angle bend with a radius of 5 times the cable diameter
It is the damage done to insulation following a voltage being applied across it.
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: It is the voltage per millimetre of insulation

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: The battery in the circuit shown has an output of 12 Volts. If the resistance of the resistor is 3 Ohms what current should be flowing in the circuit?
options: 4 Amps
4 Farads
36 Amperes
It cannot be calculated from the information given
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: 4 Amps

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: The battery in the circuit shown has an output of 6 Volts. If the resistance of the upper resistor is 3 Ohms and the current flowing in the circuit is 1 Amp then what voltage is dropped across the upper resistor according to Kirchhoff’s Law?
options: 3 Volts
2 Volts
1 Volt
It cannot be calculated from the information given
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: 3 Volts

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which one of the following best describes the primary method of protecting against overloading of an electrical conductor?
options: The conductors must be adequately rated for maximum load current under the worst environmental conditions expected
The best quality voltage overload trip must be fitted
The best quality current overload trip must be fitted
The conductors must be placed as far apart as possible
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: The conductors must be adequately rated for maximum load current under the worst environmental conditions expected

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which of the following best describes the effect of over voltage when applied to an electrical conductor?
options: It will cause insulation breakdown
It will cause thermosetting insulation to go hard
It will cause build up of static charge
It will be indicated by a colour change in the insulation
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: It will cause insulation breakdown

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which one of the following would be a typical power factor for a 440 Volt galley stove?
Which one of the following best describes what the difference is between the thermosetting and the thermoplastic insulations used on ships electrical equipment?
options: Thermoplastic insulations soften as they get warmer and thermosetting insulations do not
Thermoplastic insulations are grey and thermosetting insulations are black
Thermoplastic insulations are rigid and thermosetting insulations are not
Thermosetting insulations soften as they get warmer and thermoplastic insulations do not
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: Thermoplastic insulations soften as they get warmer and thermosetting insulations do not

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Two electrical conductors are circular in cross section and are otherwise the same except that conductor 1 has twice the diameter of conductor 2. If the resistance of conductor 1 is 2 Ohms what is the resistance of conductor 2?
options: 8 Ohms
4 Ohms
2 Ohms
1 Ohms
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: 8 Ohms

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: PVC insulated cable is very popular ashore. Which one of the following best describes the reason why it is less frequently used on ships?
options: It gives off poisonous halogen gas if on fire
Ambient temperatures on ships trading in the tropics are too high
It is expensive
It is only used on high voltage cables
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: It gives off poisonous halogen gas if on fire

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: An AC electrical circuit operates at 110 Volts. Which one of the following is the circuit’s voltage rating according to this module?
options: Low Voltage
Medium Voltage
High Voltage
Extra Low Voltage
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: Low Voltage

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which one of the following options best describes why connecting cables are usually fitted with flexible insulation?
options: Flexible insulation is necessary so connections can be made
Flexible insulation is cheaper than hard insulation
Flexible insulation is necessary so that cables can be pushed through conduit
Flexible insulation is thinner and lighter than hard insulation
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: Flexible insulation is necessary so connections can be made

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which of the following best describes the meaning of the symbol Ω when found in an electrical calculation?
options: The quantity is expressed in Ohms
It is the impedance of the component
The quantity is expressed in Coulombs
It is the resistivity of the conductor material
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: The quantity is expressed in Ohms

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Two electrical conductors are the same except that conductor 1 is four times as long as conductor 2. If the resistance of conductor 1 is 2 Ohms what is the resistance of conductor 2?
options: 0.5 Ohms
8 Ohms
2 Ohms
0.2 Ohms
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: 0.5 Ohms

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which one of the following formulas agrees with Ohms Law?
options: R = 	V/I
R = 	V.I
R = 	ρL/A
I = 	V.R
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: R = 	V/I

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: A 440 Volt AC source supplies 2 loads in parallel. The left load has an impedance of 44 Ohms and the right of 11 Ohms. Which of the following is the current taken from the AC supply?
options: 50 Amps
8 Amps
44 Amps
It cannot be calculated from the information given
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: 50 Amps

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which one of the following options best describes a significant problem with thermosetting types of insulation on ships?
options: Thermosetting insulation is not flexible and can become damaged by impacts
Thermosetting insulation is too flexible and needs excessive support
Thermosetting insulation is too expensive
Thermosetting insulation is black and hides burn marks
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: Thermosetting insulation is not flexible and can become damaged by impacts

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which one of the following describes the best way of protecting the conductors deep inside electrical machines from the effects of excessive temperature?
options: Thermistors can be built into them to sense the temperature
Bi-metallic thermal cut outs can be fitted
Clean ventilation filters on a regular basis
The current overload trip can be used
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: Thermistors can be built into them to sense the temperature

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: Which one of the following is the most common reason for a rapid rise in the current flowing through an electrical circuit, to a level many times its rated value?
options: A short circuit
Bearing failure
Excessive ambient temperature
Weakened conductors
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: A short circuit

CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.question: The basic strategy to stay alive while working with high voltage systems may be summarised as D.I.E. What does D.I.E. stand for?
options: Disconnect, Isolate, Earth
Disconnect, Isolate, Evaluate
Direct Insulation to Earth
Direction, Inertia, Evaluation
CD0230 — High Voltage, Fundamentals.answer: Disconnect, Isolate, Earth

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following options best describes the advantage industries ashore have over ships when using electrical power?
options: They can rely on a supply with voltage and frequency well controlled and redundancy provided
Their supply is close and responsive
They can select any voltage and frequency of supply they like
They can call in specialist electricians if they have a problem
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: They can rely on a supply with voltage and frequency well controlled and redundancy provided

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following options best describes what determines how much mechanical power the prime mover connected to an electrical generator must produce?
options: Enough to meet the apparent power demand and overcome mechanical losses such as friction
Enough to meet the active power demand and overcome mechanical losses such as friction
Enough to meet the reactive power demand and overcome mechanical losses such as friction
Enough to meet the active power demand and overcome electrical losses such as hysteresis
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: Enough to meet the apparent power demand and overcome mechanical losses such as friction

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following options best describes why most electric motors, driving engine room pumps, are usually supplied at around 440 Volts, even if the ship uses electricity at higher voltages for the bow thruster?
options: They tend to be near the switchboard and therefore the supply cable losses are low
The size of motors normally required for engine room pumps are only available for 440 Volt supplies
The size of motors normally required for bow thrusters are only available for high voltage supplies
Using higher voltages for the pump motors would require cables too thick to bend within the space available in the engine room
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: They tend to be near the switchboard and therefore the supply cable losses are low

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following options best describes why batteries, using chemical generation, are not currently used for the main source of electricity on ships?
options: Batteries cannot store much energy
Batteries are expensive to buy in the quantities required
Batteries produce a low cell voltage
Batteries produce DC electricity
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: Batteries cannot store much energy

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes why physical forces can be created from the interaction of 2 magnets?
options: The magnets move to make the lines of magnetic flux as short as possible
The magnets move because of an electrical charge stored within them
The magnets move to even out the flux density
The magnets move if the lines of magnetic flux are forced to cross
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: The magnets move to make the lines of magnetic flux as short as possible

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Even on a large passenger ship which generates electricity at 6,000 Volts lighting is normally supplied at voltages of 220 Volts or less. Which one of the following best describes why lighting is not supplied at a higher voltage?
options: Electrical loads for lighting are low enough to allow lower voltages to be used without excessive cable losses
Lighting switches are operated by people with no electrical training
Light fittings are not available for electrical supplies over 220 Volts
High voltage lights have an annoying flicker
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: Electrical loads for lighting are low enough to allow lower voltages to be used without excessive cable losses

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes why it is preferable to use electromagnets when constructing an electrical generator, rather than permanent magnets?
options: We can control the amount of flux that electromagnets produce
The electromagnets are bigger and therefore more robust
The electromagnets are easier to shape
We need conductors around the magnets to carry the generator output
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: We can control the amount of flux that electromagnets produce

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: When a conductor is moved through a magnetic field an EMF is produced. Which one of the following is a way to increase the value of EMF produced?
options: Move the conductor more quickly
Move the conductor in circles
Change the conductor for one with a lower resistance
Change the conductor for one with a lower resistivity
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: Move the conductor more quickly

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes the main purpose of fitting reverse power protection to an electrical generator’s circuit breaker?
options: To prevent the generator driving the prime mover
To prevent the generator being run backwards
To prevent the generator circuit breaker being closed if the generator output cables are incorrectly connected
To prevent circulating currents between 2 or more generators
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: To prevent the generator driving the prime mover

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes why few merchant ships have been fitted with nuclear electrical power generation despite the increasing price of oil fuels?
options: The generation plant is quite big and very costly
Nuclear powered ships find it hard to meet SOLAS requirements
Nuclear ships need regular supplies of fuel which is hard to obtain in some countries
Nuclear ships do not contain high value materials and fetch a low price when scrapped
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: The generation plant is quite big and very costly

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: When talking about electrical power generation on ships we often refer to the ‘prime mover’. Which one of the following best describes a ‘prime mover’?
options: The device where the energy is first converted to mechanical energy
The rotor of the main generator
The rotor of the exciter for the main generator
The pump that supplies fuel during the starting of a generator after a total blackout
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: The device where the energy is first converted to mechanical energy

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: On the main switchboard cabinet for each generator there are normally instruments fitted. Which one of the following best describes the purpose of the 4 position switch often found beneath the generator voltmeter?
options: It is to check the balance of voltage between the generator’s phases
It is to turn off the meter as it is not rated for continuous use
It is to allow one meter to read the voltage of 4 different generators
It is to allow one meter to read the voltage of 2 different generators
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: It is to check the balance of voltage between the generator’s phases

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes the fundamental difference in the typical construction of a single phase generator and a 3 phase electrical generator?
options: A three phase generator has 2 more pairs of stator coils spaced 120 degrees apart than a single phase generator
A three phase generator has 2 more rotors than a single phase generator
A three phase generator has a commutator and a single phase generator does not
A three phase generator has 2 more pairs of rotor coils than a single phase generator
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: A three phase generator has 2 more pairs of stator coils spaced 120 degrees apart than a single phase generator

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which of the following best describes why the risk of serious electric shock is higher onboard ships than it is ashore?
options: The large amount of metal can provide a low resistance path to earth
A ship’s crew are not as well trained as people ashore
Voltages used on ships are higher than those used ashore
Ships tend to use an insulated neutral distribution system
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: The large amount of metal can provide a low resistance path to earth

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which of the following best describes what the result would be if earth faults occurred on 2 different phases of a ship’s 3 phase distribution system at the same time?
options: A short circuit
Two earth fault alarms sound
Two earth faults cannot occur at the same time
A long circuit
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: A short circuit

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes the primary function of a ship’s electrical distribution system?
options: To ensure that at any given point in the system the voltage and frequency are of almost rated value
To ensure that at any point in the system there is always some electricity available
To ensure that at any given point in the system there is always a voltage present
To ensure that the voltage, current and frequency are always the same at any point in the system
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: To ensure that at any given point in the system the voltage and frequency are of almost rated value

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes the main purpose of fitting under voltage protection to an electrical generator’s circuit breaker?
options: It prevents the connection of a ‘dead’ generator to a ‘live’ switchboard
It prevents the synchronisation of 2 generators with different output voltages
It prevents overcurrents being taken from a generator due to low voltage
It corrects the output voltage of a generator after a heavy load has started
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: It prevents the connection of a ‘dead’ generator to a ‘live’ switchboard

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which of the following best describes why earth faults are a common problem on ships’ electrical networks?
options: Due to the steel structure, the vibration and the wet conditions
Due to poor maintenance procedures
Due to poor crew training
They are not common as ships are not connected to earth except when in port
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: Due to the steel structure, the vibration and the wet conditions

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes why many electrical transformers are not fitted with overcurrent protection on the secondary circuit output?
options: The output from the secondary circuit is fixed in relation to the input to the transformer so it is protected by the overcurrent trip on the supply
The output from the secondary circuit is limited by the impedance of the coil
The output from the secondary circuit is limited by the magnetic inertia of the transformer core
No overcurrent protection on the secondary circuit output is used when the output is taken from more than one voltage tapping
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: The output from the secondary circuit is fixed in relation to the input to the transformer so it is protected by the overcurrent trip on the supply

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes why many modern ships are fitted with a computerised Power Management System (PMS)?
options: It can reduce crew workload and allow more precise control of the network
A PMS has been a requirement of SOLAS since 1995 for ships over 1,600 GT
SOLAS requires ships with electrical main propulsion have a PMS fitted
A PMS must be fitted where ships have 3 or more generators
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: It can reduce crew workload and allow more precise control of the network

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: The kilowatt load on the ship’s only running generator is steady but the power factor meter shows a fall from 0.9 to 0.75. Which one of the following best describes the risk that this change in power factor poses for the ship’s electrical network?
options: The increase in apparent power may cause an overcurrent trip to operate
The fuel consumption of the generator will be increased and the fuel could run out before arrival in port
The decrease in reactive power could cause supply cables to get hotter
The galley stove might burn out
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: The increase in apparent power may cause an overcurrent trip to operate

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes the general principle used when a designer is deciding the positions of automatic disconnection devices within a ship’s electrical network?
options: The higher parts of the network ‘tree’ must be protected against a fault on the lower ‘branches’
The lower ‘branches’ of the network ‘tree’ must be protected against a fault on the higher parts
Every cable must be protected at the point where power is supplied to it
Every load must be protected at the point where power is supplied to it
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: The higher parts of the network ‘tree’ must be protected against a fault on the lower ‘branches’

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: On shore it is normal practice to connect all exposed metalwork and the neutral point of the supply to earth. Which of the following best describes what normally happens on shore when an earth fault occurs?
options: A large current flows causing the overcurrent protection to disconnect the supply
A small current flows causing an earth alarm to sound
A large current flows causing an earth alarm to sound
A very small current flows until the overcurrent protection disconnects the supply
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: A large current flows causing the overcurrent protection to disconnect the supply

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes why the frequencies of 3 phase electrical generators being connected together must be ‘in phase’?
options: So that the output voltage peaks coincide
So that the firing of No. 1 cylinders on each driving diesel engine coincide
So that the current peaks coincide
So that the frequency peaks coincide
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: So that the output voltage peaks coincide

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes the main consideration when a designer selects the voltage level for a particular area of a ship’s electrical network?
options: The maximum voltage level that the equipment can withstand
The maximum voltage level available from a ship’s generator
The minimum voltage level available from a ship’s generator
The frequency of that area of the network
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: The maximum voltage level that the equipment can withstand

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: If the earth lamps on your ship looked as shown which of the following would you assume was the most likely problem?
options: An earth fault on phase ‘S’
An earth fault on phase ‘R’
An earth fault on phase ‘T’
A faulty lamp on phase ‘S’
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: An earth fault on phase ‘S’

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes why the overall system power factors tends to change while operating electrical generators on a ship?
options: It is the sum of the power factors of all the individual loads and these may vary
It increases as the generator load approaches 100% of capacity
It decreases as the generator load approaches 100% of capacity
It varies if the ship hits bad weather and pitches heavily
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: It is the sum of the power factors of all the individual loads and these may vary

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes why the overall system power factor is important when operating electrical generators on a ship?
options: It determines the total current that the generators must produce for a given active power
It determines the kilowatt load on the generators
It determines the fuel consumption of generators
The overall system power factor cannot safely exceed 0.95
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: It determines the total current that the generators must produce for a given active power

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Earth leakage circuit breakers are commonly used ashore to protect people from earth faults. Which of the following best describes why earth leakage circuit breakers have not been commonly used on ships’ electrical networks in the past?
options: Continuity of supply is preferred
Earth leakage circuit breakers are expensive
Earth leakage circuit breakers are not reliable
Earth leakage circuit breakers do not work on insulated neutral networks
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: Continuity of supply is preferred

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes the meaning of ‘discrimination’ when applied to electrical distribution systems on ships?
options: Protection devices are to ‘discriminate’ between healthy circuits and circuits with faults, shutting off only the faulty circuits
Protection devices are to ‘discriminate’ between high voltage circuits and low voltage circuits, shutting off only the low voltage circuits
Colour coding is used to ‘discriminate’ between cables with flame retardancy and those without
Colour coding is used to ‘discriminate’ between cables made with PVC and those of other materials
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: Protection devices are to ‘discriminate’ between healthy circuits and circuits with faults, shutting off only the faulty circuits

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following describes when the under voltage trip in the starter panel of an electric motor is most likely to operate?
options: During an electrical black out
After a large electrical load is started nearby in the network
As the motor is started
If the motor becomes seized
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: During an electrical black out

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following options best describes why controlling the electrical network on a ship can be more challenging than controlling a larger network ashore?
options: Ships’ electrical networks are subject to proportionately larger variations in load demand
Ships’ electrical networks are subject to the movement of the ship
Ships’ electrical networks are more complex than a network ashore
Ships’ electrical networks use more different voltages than a typical network ashore
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: Ships’ electrical networks are subject to proportionately larger variations in load demand

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes the need for cooling of 3 phase electrical transformers?
options: They need cooling due to their internal iron and copper losses
They need cooling due to their moving parts
They need cooling due to the magnetic interaction between the 3 coils
They only need cooling when the ambient temperatures go above 50°C
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: They need cooling due to their internal iron and copper losses

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: High voltage ships tend to use earthed neutral electrical networks. Which one of the following best describes how excessive fault currents are prevented in the event of an earth fault on these ships?
options: An impedance is placed in the neutral earthing line
The risk of earth faults is reduced by extra planned maintenance
Earth leakage circuit breakers are used on every circuit
An impedance is placed in each output cable from the generators
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: An impedance is placed in the neutral earthing line

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following options best describes why each feed normally leaves the section boards in a ship’s electrical network via some form of isolation?
options: To allow for maintenance on the circuit
To allow motors to be stopped remotely
To allow lights to be switched off remotely
To protect against slow overloads
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: To allow for maintenance on the circuit

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes why most ships have 3 or more generators which can provide electrical power?
options: It provides greater reliability of supply and allows more efficient operation
SOLAS requires at least 3 generators to be provided
Three smaller generators are usually cheaper than 2 large ones
Three generators allows better balance of the ship and reduced permanent list
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: It provides greater reliability of supply and allows more efficient operation

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes why we do not normally run generators that are supplying the ship's main switchboard at their maximum continuous output where their fuel efficiency is usually best?
options: There needs to be enough reserve capacity in the generating system to deal with unexpected load increases
Fuel efficiency of generators is unimportant compared to that of the main engine
Starting and stopping an extra generator to supply short term increases in load uses more fuel than running it all the time
The generators on ships are rarely able to run at maximum continuous output without breaking down
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: There needs to be enough reserve capacity in the generating system to deal with unexpected load increases

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following describes where a ‘bus tie’ might be found on a ship with a high electrical power demand?
options: In the main switchboard near the centre of the busbars
In the main switchboard near the ends of the busbars
In any distribution board which is subject to high vibration
In any starter panel which is subject to high vibration
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: In the main switchboard near the centre of the busbars

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes the main reason why ships with high voltage electrical networks do not usually have a floating neutral system?
options: It tends to produce voltage stresses on the system cables
High voltage equipment is not designed for floating neutral systems
It is essential to use earth leakage circuit breakers on high voltage supplies
High voltage networks on ships just copy shore practice
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: It tends to produce voltage stresses on the system cables

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following best describes how someone on a ship could be killed by electricity while just walking around the engine room?
options: By touching metalwork which has become live as a result of damaged insulation
By walking on metal floor plates without shoes
By walking on metal floor plates with rubber soled shoes
By touching metalwork such as starter boxes
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: By touching metalwork which has become live as a result of damaged insulation

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: A ship has a 3 phase electrical network with star connected generators and an earthed neutral point. The network line voltage is 440V and phase voltage 254V. If an earth fault occurs on one phase through a circuit of 1Ω impedance what will be the potential fault current?
options: 254 Amps
25.4 Amps
0.004 Amps
440 Amps
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: 254 Amps

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: A ship has a 3 phase electrical network with a neutral point earthed through a 200Ω resistor. The generator phase voltage is 3,000V and the synchronous impedance of the generator is  0.1Ω. ^M^MWhat will be the potential fault current if an earth fault occurs on the generator output cable?
options: 15 Amps
1500 Amps
3,000 Amps
30,000 Amps
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: 15 Amps

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following options best describes what would happen to the terminal voltage of an AC generator following a typical major load increase if no AVR was fitted?
options: The higher current through the generator windings will result in a fall in terminal voltage
The higher current through the generator windings will result in a rise in terminal voltage
The terminal voltage will not change if the generator is well designed
The terminal voltage will rise or fall, depending on the amount of field compounding
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: The higher current through the generator windings will result in a fall in terminal voltage

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following options best describes how a single device can protect against fast and slow overcurrent faults in a ship’s distribution system?
options: An inverse time/current characteristic is needed
Only a fuse can protect against both types of faults
Two separate current sensors are fitted into the single protection device
A single device cannot protect against both types of faults
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: An inverse time/current characteristic is needed

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following options best describes what will happen if the voltages of the main switchboard and incoming generator are not the same at the time of connecting the generator?
options: Large currents will flow until the voltages become equal
Large voltages will flow until the currents become equal
The generator under voltage trip will operate
The generator frequency will be forced to match the switchboard frequency
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: Large currents will flow until the voltages become equal

CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.question: Which one of the following options best describes the reason for a ship’s distribution system being arranged for preferential tripping?
options: Non essential loads are arranged to trip in order to prevent the main generator from tripping
Low power loads are tripped in preference to high power loads
Low voltage loads are tripped in preference to high voltage loads
Final sub circuits are tripped in preference to those higher in the distribution ‘tree’
CD0231 — High Voltage, Ship's electrical.answer: Non essential loads are arranged to trip in order to prevent the main generator from tripping

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following is the best definition of the term “harmonics” when used in relation to high voltage electricity?
options: Harmonics are variations in the supply waveform
Harmonics are caused by circuit breakers opening and closing repeatedly
Harmonics are vibrations in the supply cables which can crack insulation
Harmonics are the noise made by certain high voltage generators
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Harmonics are variations in the supply waveform

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following options correctly indicates the difference in size between an 800 kW electric motor supplied at 6.6 kV and another 800 kW electric motor supplied at 440 V?
options: The 6.6 kV motor is around one third of the volume of the 440 V motor
The 6.6 kV motor is around three times of the volume of the 440 V motor
They are the same volume
The 6.6 kV motor is around one tenth of the volume of the 440 V motor
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: The 6.6 kV motor is around one third of the volume of the 440 V motor

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Maintenance of high voltage equipment has been completed and the Permit to Work cancelled. Which one of the following best describes what needs to be done to put the equipment back into service?
options: A switching plan, approved by the authorised person, must be carried out
The engine room watchkeeper is told that the permit is cancelled and the equipment can be used again
The competent person will turn the supply back on before informing the watchkeeper
The competent person will remove the main circuit earth and turn the supply back on before informing the watchkeeper
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: A switching plan, approved by the authorised person, must be carried out

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes why someone on a high voltage ship may want to use a ‘multilock’?
options: Multilocks are used where more than one person wishes to ensure that a circuit breaker cannot be operated without their permission
Multilocks are used so all padlocks on circuit breakers can be opened by the same key
Multilocks are used where more than one size of circuit breaker is required to be locked using a standard size lock
Multilocks have long wires so that more than one switch can be locked off with a single lock
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Multilocks are used where more than one person wishes to ensure that a circuit breaker cannot be operated without their permission

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes why high voltage (HV) cables tend to store electrical charge?
options: HV systems are made up of two or more parallel conductors, separated by an insulator with a voltage between them, like a capacitor
HV cables are made up of many coils of conductor with a voltage between them like a capacitor
The insulation on HV cables is softer than for low voltage and creates static charge
The insulation on HV cables is harder than for low voltage and holds a static charge
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: HV systems are made up of two or more parallel conductors, separated by an insulator with a voltage between them, like a capacitor

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: After maintenance of high voltage equipment has been completed the person carrying out the work is often asked to sign the Permit to Work before the permit is cancelled. Which one of the following best describes what the person is signing for?
options: That all tools, test equipment and any additional earths have been removed
To confirm that he knows the permit is cancelled
To record the time at which he surrendered the permit
So that the signatures can be compared before and after permit issue
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: That all tools, test equipment and any additional earths have been removed

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes the function of the insulating hooks often found near high voltage electrical switchboards?
options: They are used to remove an unconscious person from areas near high voltage electricity
They are used to dissipate high voltage electricity
They are used to test high voltage conductors to see if they are dead
They are used to form a barrier between workers and nearby high voltage sources
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: They are used to remove an unconscious person from areas near high voltage electricity

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: With regard to the management of high voltage electrical systems, which one of the following best describes the difference between an ‘Authorised Person’ and a ‘Senior Authorised Person’, as stated in this module?
options: An Authorised Person may have control over certain parts of the network with overall network control being held by a Senior Authorised Person
Only a certified Chief Engineer can be a Senior Authorised Person
Senior Authorised Persons need to reach the standards set out in STCW for electrical officers and Authorised Persons can be engineers
An Authorised Person can become a Senior Authorised Person after 18 months sea service
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: An Authorised Person may have control over certain parts of the network with overall network control being held by a Senior Authorised Person

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: If isolation is not thorough, which of the following is the most dangerous stage in making a piece of high voltage electrical equipment safe to work on, according to this module?
options: Earthing
Disconnection
Reconnection
Deading
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Earthing

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes the main advantage in using high voltage electricity through a ‘step up’ system from low voltage generators?
options: Most of the electrical system will operate at familiar voltages
Low voltage generators are smaller than high voltage ones
A high voltage fault can not affect the essential low voltage consumers
Most of the system is made up of low voltage components which are cheap
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Most of the electrical system will operate at familiar voltages

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes what will happen if a low impedance connection is accidently created across a charged capacitor within a high voltage electrical network?
options: Large amounts of power can be quickly discharged
A small amount of A.C. power can be discharged
A large amount of A.C. power can be stored
A small leakage current will flow
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Large amounts of power can be quickly discharged

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes why the earth connections applied to high voltage circuits while maintenance is being carried out are of much larger diameter than those typically used in low voltage lighting circuits?
options: The prospective earth fault currents on high voltage are much larger and the connection must be large enough not to fuse
Earth faults on high voltage need larger diameter earth connections with low resistance to allow the current to flow freely
The earth connections must be the same diameter as the current carrying conductors being earthed in both cases
Owners of high voltage systems can afford the more expensive, thicker copper earth connections
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: The prospective earth fault currents on high voltage are much larger and the connection must be large enough not to fuse

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes the meaning of the term ‘disconnected’ in relation to high voltage electrical systems?
options: The connection of power supply to the equipment has been broken
The power supply cables to the equipment have been removed from the contactor terminals and taped up
The equipment is safe to work on
There is an open circuit in at least one supply conductor to a piece of equipment
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: The connection of power supply to the equipment has been broken

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes why it is normal practice to place the high voltage (Hi-pot) tester back in its test unit after a circuit has been tested as being dead?
options: To make sure it is still working correctly
To protect the ceramic end of the tester
To make sure the test unit reading agrees with the circuit reading
To make sure the test unit batteries are still working
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: To make sure it is still working correctly

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: You have been appointed the Competent Person for checking a high voltage motor of a cargo pump. While accompanying the Authorised Person you see that the high voltage (Hi-pot) tester shows a voltage is present when the motor is being tested to see if it is dead. The voltage falls away to zero within 2 seconds. Which one of the following best describes what you should do before signing the Permit to Work to say that you are satisfied with the safety arrangements?
options: You should ask for the motor to be retested before you sign the permit , even though the reading indicates the probable successful dissipation of inductive charge
You must definitely not sign the permit as the motor is not properly isolated
You should check the batteries in the Hi-pot tester test unit
You should start the work carefully but not sign the permit or any industrial injury claim will fail
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: You should ask for the motor to be retested before you sign the permit , even though the reading indicates the probable successful dissipation of inductive charge

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes the reason for ‘dissipating’ charge from high voltage electrical systems?
options: Stored electrical charge must be drained away from equipment after it has been ‘isolated’ to make it ‘discharged’
A charge must be applied to equipment in order to test its function
A charge must be applied to equipment in order to test its insulation resistance
A charge must be transferred to the equipment using transformer action between coils
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Stored electrical charge must be drained away from equipment after it has been ‘isolated’ to make it ‘discharged’

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: The electrician has been issued with a Permit to Work on the high voltage thruster starter. Which one of the following best describes why he may also require a Sanction to Test Permit?
options: The circuit cannot be energised for testing while a Permit to Work is in force
High voltage insulation testers are very expensive and can only be issued by the stores to someone holding a Sanction to Test Permit
No testing of any kind is allowed on high voltage systems without a Sanction to Test Permit
A Sanction to Test is needed when testing high voltage circuits which run outside the main engine room
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: The circuit cannot be energised for testing while a Permit to Work is in force

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: You have been appointed the Competent Person for checking a high voltage distribution cable. While accompanying the authorised person you see that the high voltage (Hi-pot) tester shows a voltage is present when the cable is tested to see if it is dead. ^MWhich one of the following best describes the action you should take?
options: Immediately move away from the live parts, making sure no other persons will be at risk of electrocution
Get the authorised person to test the Hi-pot tester in its test unit
Change the batteries in the Hi-pot tester
Keep the Hi-pot tester in place until the voltage dissipates, or for 2 minutes, whichever is shorter
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Immediately move away from the live parts, making sure no other persons will be at risk of electrocution

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following describes the best way for the person assigned to carry out work on high voltage equipment to ensure that the switching plan has been properly carried out?
options: They should go with the person doing the switching to ensure that the plan has been completed
They should check the signature of the person doing the switching is on the Permit to Work
They should check the signature of the person doing the switching is on the Sanction to Test
They should count the number of keys in the electrician’s key safe
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: They should go with the person doing the switching to ensure that the plan has been completed

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes the main reason why the azimuth thrusters used for propulsion on some ships are normally supplied with high voltage electricity?
options: High voltage allows the azimuth thrusters to be kept small, so reducing hull resistance
High voltages remove the need for transformers to be installed on the ship
High voltage allows the azimuth thrusters to be larger, so a larger propeller can be fitted
Azimuth thrusters are only fitted on passenger ships where high voltage is available
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: High voltage allows the azimuth thrusters to be kept small, so reducing hull resistance

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes the meaning of the term ‘tracking’ when applied to high voltage electrical systems?
options: It is a noticeable current that flows through dirt on the surface of insulation
It is the method of securing busbars within a switchboard
It is a current that flows within insulation layers
It is the method of separating busbars within a switchboard
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: It is a noticeable current that flows through dirt on the surface of insulation

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following describes the best way for the person assigned to carry out work on high voltage equipment to ensure that the equipment will remain dead until their Permit to Work is withdrawn?
options: Keep the lock keys to all the isolating breakers under their control
Keep the lock keys to all the isolating breakers in the control room
Take the control fuses out of all the isolating breakers
Disconnect the output cables from all the isolating breakers
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Keep the lock keys to all the isolating breakers under their control

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes what someone issued with a Limitation of Access Permit is allowed to do in relation to high voltage electrical systems?
options: They are allowed to enter an area where access to high voltage equipment is normally restricted
They are allowed to enter and operate equipment within a restricted high voltage switchboard room
They are allowed to enter engine rooms containing high voltage propulsion motors
They are allowed to climb on top of high voltage equipment which is more than 2 metres high
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: They are allowed to enter an area where access to high voltage equipment is normally restricted

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes why extra care should be taken when preparing a high voltage transformer circuit to be worked on after it has been fully isolated?
options: The transformer contains a lot of inductance and may still hold a deadly charge
The transformer contains a lot of capacitance and may still hold a deadly charge
The transformer may be supplied from high voltage and low voltage sides
High voltage transformers are normally oil filled and may leak toxic oil
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: The transformer contains a lot of inductance and may still hold a deadly charge

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes why it is necessary to record insulation readings taken from high voltage equipment after a fixed period of test time?
options: There are 3 currents created when testing, all of which vary over time
It is advisable to ensure any undetected charge has decayed before taking a reading
The electronics within the meter need to warm up before an accurate reading is produced
The equipment gets warm while the test current is present, so changing the reading
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: There are 3 currents created when testing, all of which vary over time

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes the possible effect of the air between conductors becoming ionised?
options: Current arcs can continue to flow after the minimum safe separation is regained
Current arcs can form if the conductors move towards each other
“Ball” arcs can appear
Cable insulation can become cracked as the ionisation effects its make up
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Current arcs can continue to flow after the minimum safe separation is regained

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes the possible effect of supplying a solid insulator with a voltage above that for which it was designed?
options: Its insulating ability may be permanently reduced
Its insulating ability will only be temporarily reduced
Its insulating ability will not be affected provided that the voltage is no more than 150% of the rated voltage
Its insulating ability can be temporarily improved
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Its insulating ability may be permanently reduced

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes why, when taking insulation readings from high voltage cables, the reading is poor to start with but usually gets better quite quickly?
options: Initially there is a capacitance charging current which shows as a low resistance
The cable insulation gets warm while the test current is present, so changing the reading
The test current takes a while to stabilise as the meter batteries build up a high voltage output
The electronics within the meter need to warm up before an accurate reading is produced
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Initially there is a capacitance charging current which shows as a low resistance

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following is normally the first person to touch the conductors of high voltage equipment after they have been made safe to work on?
options: The person issuing the Permit to Work
The person issuing the Limitation of Access Permit
The Competent Person
The senior engineer on watch
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: The person issuing the Permit to Work

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following is the main reason why you may be sent to stay with the motorman while he paints the high voltage switchboard room?
options: To ensure the motorman does not touch any of the local controls on the switchboards
To ensure that the switchboards are properly covered against paint splashes
To ensure that no paint is allowed to enter the switchboard vents
To ensure that any warning signs are put back exactly where they were before painting
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: To ensure the motorman does not touch any of the local controls on the switchboards

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes the action to take if the polarisation index calculated from insulation readings on a piece of high voltage equipment has risen by 35% in 6 months?
options: The change should be investigated unless maintenance is known to be responsible for the rise
Pat yourself on the back for a good job done
Take the readings again, there must be a mistake
Send an e mail to the company telling them the new insulation meter is better than the old one
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: The change should be investigated unless maintenance is known to be responsible for the rise

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which of the following is the voltage above which electricity is considered to be high voltage according to this module?
options: 1,000 Volts A.C.
1,000 Volts D.C.
3,000 Volts A.C.
250 Volts A.C. or D.C.
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: 1,000 Volts A.C.

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Insulation readings for high voltage equipment are sometimes used to calculate a polarisation index.^M^MWhich one of the following is the value of polarisation index which is normally considered to be the lowest acceptable before investigation of the condition of the insulation is recommended?
Which one of the following best describes the process of drawing up and implementing a switching plan when connecting or disconnecting high voltage electrical equipment?
options: Anyone can draw up the switching plan but the authorised person must approve it
The authorised person must draw up the switching plan
The authorised person must draw up the switching plan but the chief engineer must approve the plan
The competent person must approve the switching plan
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Anyone can draw up the switching plan but the authorised person must approve it

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: When measuring the insulation resistance of high voltage equipment a ‘polarisation index’ test may be used. Which one of the following best describes what a ‘polarisation index’ is?
options: It is the ratio of insulation reading obtained after 10 minutes of testing divided by the reading obtained after 1 minute of testing
It is the ratio of insulation reading obtained after 1 minute of testing divided by the reading obtained after 10 minutes of testing
It is the angle between the central axis of a rotor and the indicated North of a compass needle while a test voltage is applied to the rotor windings
It is the strength of polarising lens that is necessary to see the magnetic field of the equipment under test
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: It is the ratio of insulation reading obtained after 10 minutes of testing divided by the reading obtained after 1 minute of testing

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes what you should do after you have got together the protective, test or other equipment which is to be used during work on a high voltage electrical system?
options: It must be carefully examined for visual defects before use
It must all have a test certificate which was issued less than 12 months before
Personal protective equipment must have its insulation resistance checked in at least 2 places per item
Test equipment must have its batteries checked
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: It must be carefully examined for visual defects before use

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which of the following best describes one of the most important reasons for using high voltage electricity on a ship?
options: High voltages may be necessary to limit fault currents to manageable levels
High voltages may reduce earth currents to manageable levels
High voltages may increase the power of main electric propulsion motors
High voltages may remove the need for the use of D.C. in high power systems
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: High voltages may be necessary to limit fault currents to manageable levels

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes the role of fresh air within high voltage switchboards?
options: Fresh air can be used as an insulator between suitably spaced busbars
Fresh air is used to cool high voltage circuit breaker contacts during faults
Fresh air is often removed from high voltage switchboards to create a vacuum
Fresh air is often dried before being supplied to high voltage switchboards
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Fresh air can be used as an insulator between suitably spaced busbars

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes why it is important for someone to read the detailed risk assessment for the job before they start work on high voltage equipment?
options: So they are aware of the dangers that have been identified and the safety measures in place
So they can see exactly what they need to do to complete the job efficiently
So they can see who should issue the Electrical Permit to Work
So they can see if a Limitation of Access Permit will be required
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: So they are aware of the dangers that have been identified and the safety measures in place

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Some insulation test meters for high voltage equipment are fitted with a 3rd lead, often called a ‘guard’. Which one of the following best describes the reason for using the guard lead?
options: The guard lead cuts down leakage currents which can give a falsely low insulation reading
The guard lead cuts down absorption currents which can give a falsely high insulation reading
The guard lead cuts down the risk of electrocution from the meter
The guard lead is used to check for a good earth connection
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: The guard lead cuts down leakage currents which can give a falsely low insulation reading

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Which one of the following best describes a method which can be used to continuously monitor high voltage electrical machinery for insulation condition?
options: A partial discharge monitor
Earth lights
A power factor meter
A vibration monitor
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: A partial discharge monitor

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: You are carrying out an internal examination of a high voltage switchboard. Which one of the following best describes the faults that might be detected using your sense of smell?
options: Excessive arcing, overheating, burning and leakage from some types of circuit breaker
Insulation breakdown, excessive voltage
Tracking
Loose connections, wrong type of terminations used
CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.answer: Excessive arcing, overheating, burning and leakage from some types of circuit breaker

CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: On low voltage electrical systems insulation is normally tested using voltages above the normal rated supply voltage of the equipment. CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: Your ship has been sent a circular from the company warning of problems on the distribution boards on your sister ship. CD0232 — High Voltage, Equipment and tes.question: When working on high voltage electrical equipment 3 phase portable earthing connectors might be fitted. In what order should these be connected?

CD0233 — High Voltage, Management on Shi.question: Which one of the following best describes the difference between an Authorised Person (AP) and a Senior Authorised Person (SAP)?

CD0233 — High Voltage, Management on Shi.question: Can HV sub-station (P) be supplied via the Starboard side of the ring main while the Port side is isolated?

CD0233 — High Voltage, Management on Shi.question: In relation to high voltage electrical networks, which one of the following best describes the most likely place to find a circuit main earth?

CD0233 — High Voltage, Management on Shi.question: A joint between one supply cable conductor and its terminal on a 6.6 kiloVolt electric motor has a resistance of 2 milli-Ohms. If a short circuit current of 20,000 Amps flows through the joint how much heat is generated at the joint?

CD0233 — High Voltage, Management on Shi.question: In relation to high voltage electrical equipment, which one of the following best describes the purpose of a ‘Limitation of Access’ Permit?
