Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: Each ship shall keep a ship specific Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan on board

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: If the Energy Efficiency Operational Indicator (EEOI) is used for the quantitative measurement of a ship’s energy efficiency, which one of the following measurement tools may also be used?
options: Energy audits and consumption surveys
Personal tracking devices
Archived historic maintenance records
Port State Control inspection data
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: Energy audits and consumption surveys

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: Is there a legal requirement for ships of 400 gross tonnage and above to have a Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan?
options: Yes
No
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: Yes

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: Where is the legal requirement to have a Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP) defined?
options: Annex VI of MARPOL
Part A of SOLAS
“Energy Efficiency and Fuel Management” (OCIMF)
The International Energy Efficiency Certificate
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: Annex VI of MARPOL

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: Which area of regulation has led to the focus on Energy Efficiency and the development of the Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP)?
options: Pollution Prevention
Maritime Safety
Human Factors
International Trade
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: Pollution Prevention

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: Which one of the following techniques is the most likely way that a saving in fuel consumption could be achieved as a vessel departs port or leaves an estuary?
options: By gradually increasing the speed whilst keeping the engine load within acceptable limits
By increasing to full sea speed as soon as possible
By maintaining the speed 10-15% under optimum level for the first 24 hours
By maintaining the engine load 10-15% under optimum level for the first 12 hours
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: By gradually increasing the speed whilst keeping the engine load within acceptable limits

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: When considering potential energy efficiency measures in ship design, fuel cell technology delivers an average thermal efficiency of 60%, but what design feature helps to make this figure so high?
options: The systematic minimisation of heat and mechanical loss
The use of light alloy metals in the construction of the machinery
The increasing availability of refueling stations
Harmonization with the demands of an Integrated Navigation and Command System
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: The systematic minimisation of heat and mechanical loss

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: As quoted in this training module, what is the other name by which “Just in Time” planning is known when used to optimise the ship’s speed as part of voyage planning and fuel-efficient operations?
options: Virtual Arrival
Virtual Departure
Virtual Planning
Optimum Arrival
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: Virtual Arrival

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: What does optimum speed mean in the context of fuel-efficient operations?
options: The speed at which the fuel used per tonne mile is at a minimum level for that voyage
The speed at which the fuel consumed is closest to the voyage average
The speed at which the fuel consumption is closest to that  calculated as the optimum rate in the voyage plan
The speed at which the fuel used per nautical mile is at a minimum level for that vessel
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: The speed at which the fuel used per tonne mile is at a minimum level for that voyage

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: In order to maintain efficiency, how should the propulsion system of a vessel be maintained?
options: In accordance with manufacturers' instructions and as part of the company's planned maintenance schedule
With minimal intrusive action
On a reactive basis only
As required to maintain all Classification Society and Flag State certificates valid and free of notations
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: In accordance with manufacturers' instructions and as part of the company's planned maintenance schedule

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: By what type of method, as explained in this training module, should the energy efficiency of a ship be measured?
options: By an established method, preferably an international standard
By any appropriate method, provided it has IMO approval
By the IEEC standard evaluation method
By any method the  Master deems appropriate
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: By an established method, preferably an international standard

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: What do the letters EEOI stand for in relation to the management of energy aboard ship?
options: Energy Efficiency Operational Indicator
Environmental Energy Optimum Index
Energy Emission  Operator  Interpolation
Energy Efficient Operation Implementation
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: Energy Efficiency Operational Indicator

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: In addition to both the company and the ship developing procedures for energy efficiency management and defining tasks as part of the Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP), which of the following must also be done?
options: The tasks must be assigned to qualified personnel
The procedures must be approved as part of the IEEC application process
Nothing – this is all that is required as part of a SEEMP
The procedures and tasks must be tested and the results recorded before the SEEMP is submitted for approval
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: The tasks must be assigned to qualified personnel

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: From the outset of the planning and implementation of a SEEMP, the company should seek to integrate the relevant parts of which one of the following into its general ship management operations?
options: The Corporate Energy Efficiency Management Plan
The Company Cargo Operations Manual
The Fleet Management Procedures
The Company Environmental Protection Policy
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: The Corporate Energy Efficiency Management Plan

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: What should the self-evaluation and improvement step of a Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP) deliver?
options: Meaningful feedback for the first step of the next SEEMP cycle
Quantitative analysis enabling close-out of the SEEMP
Data on a ship’s energy consumption
A conclusive index position by which a company’s energy management policy can be rated by the flag State Authority
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: Meaningful feedback for the first step of the next SEEMP cycle

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: What sort of process is associated with a Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP)?
options: One of continuous improvement through successive cycles of the plan
A one-off application leading to the issuing of an International Energy Efficiency Certificate
One that includes re-submission to the Flag State Authority every 10 years
The processes associated with a SEEMP are all defined and regulated by the individual ship’s senior personnel
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: One of continuous improvement through successive cycles of the plan

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: What is the purpose of a Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP)?
options: It is a management tool to assist ship-owners or managers in managing the energy efficiency of their ships
To train ship’s crews in operational practices
To provide suitable evidence on a Flag State inspection
To reduce P&I insurance premiums
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: It is a management tool to assist ship-owners or managers in managing the energy efficiency of their ships

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: Which one of the following must a Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP) be?
options: Ship-specific
Company-specific
Fleet-specific
Flag State specific
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: Ship-specific

CD0258 — SEEMP.question: As part of an Energy Efficiency Management policy, which one of the following might reasonably be expected as a result of an on-board awareness campaign together with training on the fundamentals of the Management Plan?
options: That the various energy efficiency options implemented by the company are understood
That the fuel consumption calculations for the vessel are fully understood by the engine ratings
That  less detailed voyage planning is  required
That the crew understand that the SEEMP is  a confidential document and should not be made available to Port State authorities
Incorrect
Correct
CD0258 — SEEMP.answer: That the various energy efficiency options implemented by the company are understood

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: The concept of culture is often illustrated as an onion consisting of three layers. What does the innermost layer consist of?
options: It consists of the fundamental beliefs expressed through our actions, our behaviour and how we interact with others.
It consists of the artefacts of the culture, which is the physical evidence of a culture like signs, furniture, rituals, language, meetings etc.
It consists of the procedures, written rules, campaign posters and reporting systems.
It consists of the expressed values of a culture like policies, and norms and values to be followed in the organisation.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: It consists of the fundamental beliefs expressed through our actions, our behaviour and how we interact with others.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: The risk management process can be divided into three levels; organisational level, risk management level, individual level. Which one of the given options best describes the level or levels typically overlooked and the mindset that should be adopted?
options: The individual level is typically overlooked. The mindset to adopt is that every individual is responsible for safety and should not only rely on procedures, but should make their own risk assessment of the present situation prior to any work task.
The risk management level is typically overlooked. The mindset to adopt is that prior to every work task a formal risk assessment should be made by every individual and discussed in teams.
The Organisational level is typically overlooked. The mindset to adopt is that the organisation is responsible for the safety and therefore all procedures should be followed at all times.
All three levels are typically overlooked. The mindset to adopt is that at least one of the levels should be addressed prior to any work task.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: The individual level is typically overlooked. The mindset to adopt is that every individual is responsible for safety and should not only rely on procedures, but should make their own risk assessment of the present situation prior to any work task.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options best describes the mindset that must be in place on the highest level of a safety maturity ladder?
options: Safety is a way of thinking, working and running the business and the safety aspect is part of every work related consideration.
Accidents are considered part of the job and the safety responsibility is placed in the safety department.
It is important to involve the staff and to develop the individual’s responsibility for the safety work.
Safety is defined as compliance with rules and procedures. When accidents happen several actions are initiated to avoid recurrence.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Safety is a way of thinking, working and running the business and the safety aspect is part of every work related consideration.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options is the main reason why it is always important to follow up on safety behaviour modification feedback?
options: Because changing behaviour is like developing new habits - it requires continuous follow-up.
Because the captain needs to be informed about the result of the feedback.
Because it is a requirement in the SMS-system.
Because it is important for knowledge sharing between the crew.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Because changing behaviour is like developing new habits - it requires continuous follow-up.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the following statements best describes why it is important to observe and modify safety behaviour?
options: Good safety behaviour at a workplace creates a strong overall safety culture.
It is important to ensure a good flow in the reporting system, so that shore based staff can take appropriate actions.
So that unsafe actions can be reported.
It is important because it is a requirement in the ISM code.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Good safety behaviour at a workplace creates a strong overall safety culture.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the actions in the options given is most likely to reveal why the feedback advice given to an employee was not followed by the employee?
options: Asking the employee questions and being enquiring in the approach.
Being appreciative and highlighting the positives in the outcome.
Discussing the situation at a management meeting onboard.
Asking the employee’s colleagues the reasons.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Asking the employee questions and being enquiring in the approach.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options best describes who has responsibility for the safety onboard?
options: Everybody holds the responsibility for the safety onboard. Everybody should react upon poor and unsafe safety behaviour and conditions whether it involves a subordinate, a colleague or a superior.
The captain holds the responsibility for safety on board ship. Anyone experiencing unsafe behaviour should therefore report it to the captain immediately.
Each person only has responsibility for their own safety. Being aware of their own safety behaviour is vital for overall safety on board.

Only supervisors have responsibility for safety onboard. It is their responsibility to react to unsafe or poor safety behaviour and conditions by intervening, stopping or correcting the actions of subordinates.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Everybody holds the responsibility for the safety onboard. Everybody should react upon poor and unsafe safety behaviour and conditions whether it involves a subordinate, a colleague or a superior.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options is an example of the simple ethics described in this module that should be followed when doing an observation?
options: Be well prepared, be enquiring in your approach, build on the relationship, provide immediate feedback.
Ensure that the captain is assisting you in the observation, write down both good and poor working conditions, provide feedback in writing as soon as possible after the observation.
Always have at least three persons doing the observation to avoid details being overlooked, don’t get too friendly with the people you observe.
Prepare the observation by reviewing important procedures and ask the person who is being observed what they want you to observe.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Be well prepared, be enquiring in your approach, build on the relationship, provide immediate feedback.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the options below best describes what should be observed when it comes to safety condition and behaviour?
options: Incorrect use of tools and equipment, violations of procedures, incorrect body use, poor housekeeping.
If the crewmember knows the ISM code in detail and if procedures are followed no matter what.
If the crew member attends at least one safety meeting a year.
If the crew member is familiar with the maintenance and emergency plans.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Incorrect use of tools and equipment, violations of procedures, incorrect body use, poor housekeeping.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the options given below best describes why it is important to track barriers to safe behaviour?
options: Because identification of barriers to safety makes it possible to start actions to remove those barriers and thereby make safe behaviour more likely and logical.
Because tracking barriers to safety is part of the SMS.
Because tracking barriers to safety gives management a chance to monitor the crew.
Because identification of barriers to safety provides an indication if procedures need to be changed.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Because identification of barriers to safety makes it possible to start actions to remove those barriers and thereby make safe behaviour more likely and logical.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options correctly completes the following statement? ‘Situational awareness is...
options: ...the responsibility of all crew members’
...only the responsibility of the officer in charge’
...only the responsibility of the cadet and able seaman’
...the responsibility of the company’
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: ...the responsibility of all crew members’

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which of the given options is the first of the 7 principles of corrective feedback necessary to reach the desired result?
options: The first step to reach the desired result is to act quickly.
The first step to reach the desired result is to be clear and direct.
The first step to reach the desired result is to set direction to improve behaviour.
The first step to reach the desired result is to take ownership.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: The first step to reach the desired result is to act quickly.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options describes the arrangement for feedback that is most likely to drive performance?
options: It should be informal, daily and constructive.
It should be provided by the captain.
It should be scheduled to take place every month at a meeting.
It should be given as a written plan where the employee can add their own ideas.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: It should be informal, daily and constructive.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: The process of observing safety conditions and behaviour (SCBO) is split into a number of sequential steps. Which of the given options fully identifies these steps?
options: Define and specify what to observe, prepare the observation, observe, intervene and provide corrective feedback and follow-up on actions.
Identify the safety issues from last observation, discuss the improvements, observe present situation and intervene and provide corrective feedback.
Define and specify improvements, observe safety conditions and behaviour, provide corrective feedback and follow-up on actions.
Observe, intervene and provide corrective feedback and follow-up on actions.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Define and specify what to observe, prepare the observation, observe, intervene and provide corrective feedback and follow-up on actions.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Consider a situation where you are working in a team. Who is responsible for the situational awareness of the team?
options: Everyone involved in the job is responsible for the situational awareness relevant to their duties and responsibilities.
The Master of the vessel is always responsible for all situational awareness, as they are in charge of the vessel.
The Company or owner is responsible for situational awareness as they are financially in charge.
The officer in charge of the team is solely responsible for the situational awareness as he is the supervisor.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Everyone involved in the job is responsible for the situational awareness relevant to their duties and responsibilities.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options best describes why personal responsibility cannot be eliminated by procedures, equipment and generic risk assessments?
options: Because equipment, written generic procedures and risk assessments cannot capture all the relevant details of the current situation.
Because generic procedures and risk assessments are often made several years ago and therefore not updated in accordance with new equipment.
Because written generic procedures and risk assessments are written only to comply with the ISM code and do not contain relevant details about the current situation.
Because equipment and written generic procedures and risk assessments cannot protect you from the act of new and inexperienced crew on board.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Because equipment, written generic procedures and risk assessments cannot capture all the relevant details of the current situation.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which of the given options best describes the main difference between situational awareness and risk assessment?
options: The difference between situational awareness and risk assessment is that situational awareness is informal.
The difference between situational awareness and risk assessment is that situational awareness can only be used in certain situations.
The difference between situational awareness and risk assessment is that risk assessment can only be used in certain situations.
The difference between situational awareness and risk assessment is that risk assessment is informal.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: The difference between situational awareness and risk assessment is that situational awareness is informal.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options best describes the characteristics of an intervention culture?
options: It relies on peer-to-peer influence.
It relies on the captain’s influence.
It relies on the influence of superiors.
It relies on top down influence.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: It relies on peer-to-peer influence.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options identifies the five good safety behaviour patterns to strive for in creating a strong safety culture?
options: Proactiveness, assertiveness, involving, visibility, knowledge-based actions.
Proactiveness, influence, appreciative, hands-on, knowledge-based actions.
Assertiveness, integration, knowledge-based actions, involving, visibility.
Assertiveness, knowledge-based actions, visibility, influence, intervention.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Proactiveness, assertiveness, involving, visibility, knowledge-based actions.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options best describes the value of a formal and structured safety condition and behaviour observation?
options: It allows you to reflect, select and prioritise key areas to observe, to prepare and structure your observation and to write down important findings to be addressed.
It allows you to prepare everybody on the ship in order for them to improve prior to the observation.
It allows you to ask for assistance and back-up from the captain and the office staff and to check the SMS-system for updates.
It allows you to write down all the safety issues you believe should be addressed during the observation and to make plans for improvements.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: It allows you to reflect, select and prioritise key areas to observe, to prepare and structure your observation and to write down important findings to be addressed.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options best describes the process that the crew must be able to manage as part of developing a good safety culture?
options: The process of observing, identifying and correcting unsafe behaviour, conditions and attitudes.
The process of observing unsafe behaviour, conditions and attitudes.
The process of identifying and note down unsafe behaviour, conditions and attitudes.
The process of reporting unsafe behaviour, conditions and attitudes.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: The process of observing, identifying and correcting unsafe behaviour, conditions and attitudes.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options identifies a factor that should be observed when observing safety behaviour?
options: Working conditions should also be observed, since poor working conditions can have a strong influence on people’s behaviour.
Maintenance work should always be chosen when observing behaviour, as most accidents happen during this type of work.
Mooring operations should always be observed as they involve many crewmembers at a time.
The competence management system should also be addressed as the level of professional skills has a high impact on safety behaviour.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Working conditions should also be observed, since poor working conditions can have a strong influence on people’s behaviour.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options best explains why safety communication is important?
options: Ongoing verbal and visible safety communication is an effective way to develop a good safety culture and to communicate that safety is top priority of the company.
A company’s safety culture benefits from regular newsletters about safety. Employees should then be updated on new updates in the SMS-system, which will influence their attitude towards safety.
A company’s safety culture is defined by the number of safety meetings on board, where safety reports are addressed and discussed.
Monthly safety discussions are important for the attitude towards safety on board. Employees respond to formal meetings where safety is on the agenda.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Ongoing verbal and visible safety communication is an effective way to develop a good safety culture and to communicate that safety is top priority of the company.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the given options has been identified in the module as one of the key elements of safety communication?
options: Feedback is an essential tool in safety communication and safety should be addressed daily and integrated into every operational activity.
The safety procedures are an essential tool in safety communication, and safety discussions should always take place in a formal meeting.
Weekly observations are an essential tool in safety communication and safety should be addressed prior to all routine operations.
Corrective feedback is an essential tool in safety communication and lists of reported safety issues should be put on notice boards to ensure improvements.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: Feedback is an essential tool in safety communication and safety should be addressed daily and integrated into every operational activity.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Which one of the statements given in the options best describes what you need to do in preparation for giving corrective feedback?
options: In order to prepare for corrective feedback you need a clear idea of the desired result.
In order to prepare for corrective feedback you need to confer with the Company’s SMS Circular about corrective feedback.
In order to prepare for corrective feedback you first need the Master’s approval.
In order to prepare for corrective feedback you first need to make a list of the items the employee has done wrong.
CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.answer: In order to prepare for corrective feedback you need a clear idea of the desired result.

CD0260 — Behaviour based safety.question: Accidents rates can best be reduced by:

options: True
False

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Which one of the given options describes how mentoring can help the officer of the watch (OOW) to understand the correct avoiding action to take in compliance with the regulations for preventing collisions (coll regs)?
options: Mentoring helps the OOW better understand the practical application of the coll regs
Mentoring will always assist by telling the OOW what action to take in each case
Mentoring will make the OOW comply with the coll regs
Mentoring cannot help with practical knowledge of the coll regs
CD0261 — Mentoring.answer: Mentoring helps the OOW better understand the practical application of the coll regs

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Senior officers should always monitor interpersonal relationships between crew members’.
options: False
True

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘As a result of mentoring, a junior officer can have performance that equates to a senior officer’.
options: True
False

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Which one of the given options describes the result of effective mentoring?
options: Mentoring helps in matching theoretical knowledge with practical application
Mentoring is mainly used to acquire theoretical underpinning knowledge
Mentoring can provide the theoretical principles of a task only
Mentoring can effectively replace formal classroom training in all areas
CD0261 — Mentoring.answer: Mentoring helps in matching theoretical knowledge with practical application

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Indicate the correct answer to the following question. ‘Should the master take time out of his busy schedule to mentor his officers?’
options: Yes
No

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘When the mentor recaps all they have taught, it is known as reverse mentoring.’
options: False
True

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Select one option that most accurately completes the following statement. ‘To be able to effectively perform their practical role, seafarers need…
options: …some form of mentoring on board a vessel’.
…a full week of on the job training before taking over’.
…a high level of academic knowledge only’.
…to have already sailed on the vessel’.
CD0261 — Mentoring.answer: …some form of mentoring on board a vessel’.

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘A second Officer on board an operational tanker cannot possibly be both a candidate and mentor’.
options: False
True

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Which one of the given options is the most appropriate to explain the process of ‘mentoring’?
options: Mentoring occurs when two persons exchange life’s experiences
It is a classroom based method of knowledge transfers
Mentoring occurs in a team when the leader monitors the activity
Mentoring is a personal activity undertaken by reflecting on life
CD0261 — Mentoring.answer: Mentoring occurs when two persons exchange life’s experiences

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘On the job training serves as the best method of experiential knowledge transfer as it reinforces theoretical knowledge through practice’.
options: True
False

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘The 10 minute challenge is a method of monitoring the performance of others’.
options: False
True

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Which one of the given options is the most appropriate to define the term ‘candidate’?
options: A person who receives experiential knowledge from another
A person who needs physical assistance with a job in the work place
A person not able to work using their own initiative
A low ranking person on a vessel
CD0261 — Mentoring.answer: A person who receives experiential knowledge from another

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Which one of the given options is the most appropriate to define the term ‘personal reflection with respect to life’s experiences’?
options: Thoughtful and honest consideration of a person’s own experiences
A process of looking back to store good memories of personal experiences
A process of looking back to store bad memories of personal experiences
Critically reviewing the actions of another person in the work place
CD0261 — Mentoring.answer: Thoughtful and honest consideration of a person’s own experiences

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Select one of the given options that most accurately completes the following statement. ‘In order to further experiential knowledge it is important that all accident investigations are…
options: …available in a relevant language’.
…printed in the English language only’.
…kept confidential.’
…written in a technical language’.

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Which one of the given options is the most appropriate to define the term ‘mentor’?
options: A person who is an experienced and trusted adviser
A person who likes to formally teach a group of people
A person who has vast practical experience
A senior officer on a vessel
CD0261 — Mentoring.answer: A person who is an experienced and trusted adviser

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Select one appropriate option from those given which is NOT a step involved in mentoring?
options: Planning
Execution
Preparation
De-briefing

CD0261 — Mentoring.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘For effective mentoring it is necessary to communicate in a common language on a multi-national crewed ship’.
options: True
False

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following criteria can be used to determine the validity of an assessment strategy?
options: It is judged to have validity if it fully tests the stated learning objectives and no other knowledge or skills.
It is said to have validity if it fully tests the stated learning objectives and also other knowledge and skills.
It is said to have validity if it is judged to be reliable.
It is judged to have validity if good candidates achieve a 100% score
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: It is judged to have validity if it fully tests the stated learning objectives and no other knowledge or skills.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: An assessor suspects that there has been collaboration between candidates in an assessment that was intended to assess the individuals’ knowledge or skill. Which one of the following actions is most likely to determine if collaboration has taken place?
options: Verify the knowledge of the suspected candidate by oral questioning
Make all candidates take the assessment again.
Make a final judgement, based on past performance of the candidate.
Set a new assessment for the suspected candidate.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Verify the knowledge of the suspected candidate by oral questioning

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following criteria can be used to determine the reliability of an assessment?
options: Consistent scores, irrespective of the assessor,  timing of assessment or  the candidate
An equal number of candidates meeting and failing to meet the assessment criteria.
Every marker awards exactly the same score for a selected candidate.
Every candidate achieves the same score for a given assessment.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Consistent scores, irrespective of the assessor,  timing of assessment or  the candidate

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: In relation to the analyses of assessment results, which of the following can be considered necessary in order to ensure that any analyses is meaningful?
options: There should be sufficient data from different sources.
All of the data should come from an individual assessor.
All of the data should come from a single assessment occasion.
There should be no variance whatsoever between actual results and previous or expected results.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: There should be sufficient data from different sources.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Why is it important that assessors follow best practice when planning and carrying out an observational assessment?
options: It gives the candidate the best opportunity to demonstrate their proficiency.
Following best practice means that nothing will ever go wrong during an assessment.
Best practice means that there are fixed methods that work for every candidate in every situation.
A totally inexperienced assessor will always make the correct judgement if they follow best practice.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: It gives the candidate the best opportunity to demonstrate their proficiency.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select the statement which best describes how an assessor should act in relation to making a judgement of a candidate’s competence based purely on the final product or end result.
options: Competence is about how the result is achieved as well as what result is achieved and therefore a judgement regarding competence should not be made based purely on the end result or final product.
In order to achieve an acceptable final product or end result a candidate must be competent and therefore the assessor can consider it is an effective test of competence.
The only thing that really matters is the final product or end result, so if this is good then an assessor can judge a candidate as being competent.
Providing a candidate can produce the correct end result on at least one occasion, the assessor can reasonably judge them to be competent.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Competence is about how the result is achieved as well as what result is achieved and therefore a judgement regarding competence should not be made based purely on the end result or final product.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which of the following most accurately defines the term 'plagiarism' in relation to assessment of a candidate?
options: Falsely claiming work submitted for assessment is their own without the knowledge of the person it actually belongs to.
Claiming work submitted for assessment is their own work when another person has contributed to it.
It is when one candidate gives another candidate the correct answer during an examination.
It is concealing prohibited material during an examination for reference purposes.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Falsely claiming work submitted for assessment is their own without the knowledge of the person it actually belongs to.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which of the following statements is the most accurate in relation to candidates’ actions in an assessment?
options: Collaboration is both expected and acceptable during assessment of group work.
Collaboration and plagiarism are exactly the same and both are unacceptable.
Collaboration should never be allowed during any assessment.
A candidate using prohibited, concealed information during an assessment is guilty of collaboration.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Collaboration is both expected and acceptable during assessment of group work.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which of the following most accurately defines the term 'collaboration' in relation to assessment of candidates?
options: Work submitted for assessment to which individuals other than the candidate have knowingly contributed.
Claiming work submitted for assessment is their own work when another person has contributed to it.
It is when a candidate uses prohibited material during an examination.
It is concealing prohibited material during an examination for reference purposes.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Work submitted for assessment to which individuals other than the candidate have knowingly contributed.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: In relation to the assessment of seafarers, which of the following can be fully assessed using questions that require written descriptive answers?
options: Knowledge, understanding and other higher cognitive skills.
Psychomotor skills.
Affective skills.
Competence.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Knowledge, understanding and other higher cognitive skills.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: In relation to formative and summative assessment, which one of the following statements is true?
options: Formative and summative assessment can sometimes be combined for grading purposes.
Formative assessment can be used to give feedback whereas summative assessment cannot.
Summative assessment can be used to give feedback to both the learner and the assessor, unlike formative assessment.
The only purpose for using either summative or formative assessment is to grade learners.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Formative and summative assessment can sometimes be combined for grading purposes.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Bloom’s taxonomy divides skills into three domains. Which one of the domains identified in the options deals mainly with knowledge and understanding?
options: Cognitive
Affective
Psychomotor
Elective
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Cognitive

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following statements is correct in relation to the value of self assessment by a candidate during a programme of learning?
options: Self assessment can motivate a candidate to improve performance, as it provides evidence of progress and identifies where improvement can be made.
Self assessment has little value in helping to improve performance for most candidates.
Self assessment by the candidate can be used as an alternative to assessor led assessment and therefore reduces the required assessor input.
When candidates self assess their own performance they only ever identify their strengths, and therefore it has little value.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Self assessment can motivate a candidate to improve performance, as it provides evidence of progress and identifies where improvement can be made.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select, from the following, the statement which best describes the circumstances under which an onboard assessor would normally use formative assessment?
options: Only when the assessor is also the trainer.
An assessor would never use formative assessment.
An assessor would normally use formative assessment as the main way of grading a learner.
An assessor would use formative assessment before any training takes place to establish the learners existing knowledge and skills.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Only when the assessor is also the trainer.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: In relation to assessment of learners, which one of the following is usually considered as the main purpose of using summative assessment?
options: To grade the learner after training is completed.
To provide feedback to the learner.
To provide feedback to the assessor.
To grade the learner before training has started.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: To grade the learner after training is completed.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate method that an assessor can use to test a candidate’s ability to apply knowledge or understanding?
options: By setting the candidate a problem to solve or a task to complete.
By oral questioning of the candidate.
By setting a written examination.
Only by direct observation.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: By setting the candidate a problem to solve or a task to complete.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Summative assessment is usually carried out either at the end of a programme of learning or as each section of the programme is completed. Which one of the following statements is the most accurate in relation to summative assessment?
options: Summative assessment can be used to provide feedback as to the effectiveness of a programme.
Summative assessment is only used for grading of learners.
Summative assessment is mainly used to provide feedback to the learner to assist in further learning.
Summative assessment is another term for pre-assessment.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Summative assessment can be used to provide feedback as to the effectiveness of a programme.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select from the following statements the one that is the most accurate in relation to the term ‘assessment for learning’.
options: Assessment for learning is part of the learning process and provides instant feedback to the learner.
Only formative assessment can be used for the purpose of assessment for learning.
Both pre assessment and summative assessment are usually used for assessment for learning.
Assessment for learning is a process which is used solely for deciding the content of a programme of learning.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Assessment for learning is part of the learning process and provides instant feedback to the learner.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select from the following the most appropriate assessment method that can be used by an assessor to assess understanding or comprehension?
options: Direct oral or written divergent type and follow-up questions.
Direct observation of the candidate performing a practical task.
Direct oral or written convergent type questions.
Direct written questions only.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Direct oral or written divergent type and follow-up questions.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select, from the following, the phrase which correctly completes the following statement. ‘If an assessor uses an inappropriate level of language during an assessment ...
options: ...some candidates may be disadvantaged so it is unacceptable.’
...it will probably not affect the performance of any of the candidates so it is acceptable.’
...only the performance of the weakest candidates will be affected but it is still unacceptable.’
...the performance of all candidates will be affected to the same degree so it is acceptable.’
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: ...some candidates may be disadvantaged so it is unacceptable.’

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select from the following the one which is correct in relation to the importance of the timing of an assessment and the reason why it is important.
options: Assessments should only be scheduled for a time that allows both the assessor and the candidate to prepare properly.
Assessments should always be carried out in the morning, as the candidate will be less tired.
Assessments should always take place in the afternoon so that both the assessor and candidate have the morning to prepare for them.
Assessments should only be scheduled during normal working time, to avoid any additional costs.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Assessments should only be scheduled for a time that allows both the assessor and the candidate to prepare properly.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which of the following is the main reason why the duration of an assessment should be limited?
options: If an assessment lasts too long, candidates may not be able to perform to their full ability throughout.
With unlimited time, anyone will be able to pass an assessment so time should be limited.
The longer the assessment lasts, the more marking an assessor will have to do.
Candidates have to get used to keeping to limited time allowances for their work role.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: If an assessment lasts too long, candidates may not be able to perform to their full ability throughout.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select from the following the most appropriate assessment method that can be used by an assessor to assess knowledge?
options: Direct oral or written convergent type questions.
Direct observation of the candidate performing a practical task.
Direct oral or written divergent type questions.
Direct written questions are the only appropriate method.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Direct oral or written convergent type questions.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: When assessing a candidate’s affective skills, which one of the following are the best methods for an assessor to use?
options: One to one or group discussion and direct observation.
Written projects and examinations.
Direct observation and written examination.
One to one discussion and oral questions.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: One to one or group discussion and direct observation.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select, from the phrases given in the options, the one that most accurately completes the following statement. ‘An assessment strategy can be said to be valid if...
options: ...the assessment tests all the learning objectives and therefore all of the intended outcomes are fully measured.’
...the assessment tests the majority of the learning objectives and therefore a good sample of the outcomes is measured.’
...an acceptable number of candidates successfully complete each assessment test.’
...at least some of the assessment tests are related directly to the defined learning objectives.’
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: ...the assessment tests all the learning objectives and therefore all of the intended outcomes are fully measured.’

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: It is the responsibility of an assessor to ensure that the candidate is provided with full information regarding the assessment. Which one of the following statements best describes the responsibility that the candidate has regarding this information?
options: The candidate should study it prior to the assessment so that they have time to clarify any doubts with the assessor.
The candidate should study it at the beginning of the assessment so that the requirements are fresh in their mind.
The candidate should take it to the assessment with them so that they can make reference to it during the assessment.
The candidate only needs to use the information if there are any problems following the assessment.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: The candidate should study it prior to the assessment so that they have time to clarify any doubts with the assessor.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: In relation to a programme of learning, select from the following the one which identifies when formative assessment would normally take place?
options: At various stages during the programme.
Only at the beginning of the programme.
Only at the end of the programme.
At the beginning and end of the programme.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: At various stages during the programme.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select, from the following statements, the one which is the main purpose of including pre-assessment in a programme of learning?
options: To establish a learner’s existing skill or knowledge prior to a programme of learning.
To prepare learners for final, summative assessment.
To grade learners before they take on a new work role.
To reduce the number of learner’s taking part in a programme of learning.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: To establish a learner’s existing skill or knowledge prior to a programme of learning.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select from the following statements the one which is the main reason why it is important to have a suitable marking scheme for an assessment?
options: It will provide evidence of the reliability and consistency of an assessment.
It is required for quality assurance purposes.
It makes it easy to count the total available mark.
It allows all questions to be allocated equal marks, no matter how many parts there are to each question.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: It will provide evidence of the reliability and consistency of an assessment.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select, from the phrases given in the options, the one that correctly completes the following statement. ‘An assessment strategy is said to be reliable when...
options: ...assessment decisions made by different assessors are consistent for different candidates over a period of time.’
...assessment results are the same for any candidate, no matter how many times they are assessed.’
...it requires that assessors have a draft marking scheme for each assessment.’
...each year the same percentage of candidates successfully complete the assessments and obtain the same grades.’
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: ...assessment decisions made by different assessors are consistent for different candidates over a period of time.’

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: When assessing a candidate’s psychomotor skills, which one of the following is the most appropriate for an assessor to employ?
options: Direct observation of a work task.
Written tests only.
Oral questioning only.
Oral questioning and written tests.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Direct observation of a work task.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select, from the following statements, the one which is the most accurate in relation to mark allocation in an assessment marking scheme?
options: An assessor should allocate marks to each question and part of a question based on their judgement as to the importance and difficulty of the required answer.
An assessor should allocate marks to each question and part of a question based on the complexity of the wording of the question.
An assessor should allocate marks to each question and part of a question based on the expected length of the answer to each question.
An assessor should allocate marks to each question and part of a question based on the anticipated time it will take to mark the answer.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: An assessor should allocate marks to each question and part of a question based on their judgement as to the importance and difficulty of the required answer.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the phrases given in the options most accurately completes the following statement? ‘Feedback to a candidate following assessment is important because...
options: ...it should motivate the candidate by highlighting areas of strength as well as areas for improvement.’
...it is the only way to let the candidate know the result of the assessment.’
...it is usually a requirement of the assessment strategy quality assurance process.’
...it is better to offer feedback than to draw up an improvement plan for the candidate.’
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: ...it should motivate the candidate by highlighting areas of strength as well as areas for improvement.’

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select from the options given the one that best defines a learning outcome in relation to a programme of learning.
options: It is a general statement to indicate what the learner should be able to do after completing the programme.
It is a measurable, specific statement to indicate what the learner should be able to do after completing each section of the programme.
It is a general statement which describes what the assessment result should be at the end of the programme.
It is a measurable, specific statement to indicate what the learner should be able to do after completing the programme.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: It is a general statement to indicate what the learner should be able to do after completing the programme.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: STCW is the main standard used for training of seafarers and contains a series of competence tables which should be the main source for defining competence requirements. Select from the following elements of the competence tables the one that is most likely to be used to determine learning objectives?
options: The knowledge, understanding and proficiency statements.
The competence statements
The competence evaluation criteria
The methods for demonstrating competence
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: The knowledge, understanding and proficiency statements.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select, from the phrases given in the options, the one that correctly completes the following statement. ‘An assessment strategy is said to have transparency...
options: ...when the exact requirements for each assessment are clearly communicated to all candidates.’
...when all candidates are fully informed of their results for all assessments.’
...when the assessment results are made publically available to everyone.’
...when all assessors agree with the assessment methods to be used.’
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: ...when the exact requirements for each assessment are clearly communicated to all candidates.’

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: One reason why an assessor needs to produce a marking scheme when preparing an assessment is to indicate the mark allocation to the candidate. Which one of the following is another important reason for having a detailed marking scheme?
options: The assessor may not be the person who marks all of the assessments.
A detailed marking scheme is only required for quality assurance purposes.
Flag State only accepts assessment decisions based on marking schemes that they have approved.
Port State control will always require evidence of a marking scheme following any incident involving an individual who has been assessed onboard.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: The assessor may not be the person who marks all of the assessments.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following statements is the most accurate in relation to assessment of the competence of a group of candidates?
options: Assessors should consider the best methods for assessing each individual candidate in order to ensure that assessments are effective and fair.
All candidates should be assessed by exactly the same means in order to ensure fairness in the assessment.
Assessors are usually extremely busy and cannot concern themselves with individual candidate needs.
If any of the candidate’s cannot complete an assessment due to their individual characteristics then the assessor should just fail them.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Assessors should consider the best methods for assessing each individual candidate in order to ensure that assessments are effective and fair.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which of the following statements most accurately describes learning that is referred to as 'associative learning'?
options: It is when, through practice, individual skills are combined together with knowledge and understanding to demonstrate competence.
It is when a candidate helps an associate or colleague to learn.
It is the process where an improvement in language skills is associated with general learning.
It is learning based on copying the actions of associates or colleagues.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: It is when, through practice, individual skills are combined together with knowledge and understanding to demonstrate competence.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select from the options the phrase that most accurately completes the following statement. ‘A programme of learning can be defined as...
options: ...a series of activities designed to enable learners to gain further knowledge or skills or to improve existing knowledge or skills.’
...a series of lessons that is delivered in a classroom or lecture theatre involving more than one learner.’
...a course of study that is delivered through audio visual programmes at the learner’s workplace.’
...one lesson from a series of computer based training programmes designed for self study.’
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: ...a series of activities designed to enable learners to gain further knowledge or skills or to improve existing knowledge or skills.’

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the phrases given in the options correctly completes the following statement? ‘Associative learning is improved by feedback from assessment which...
options: ...encourages a learner to practice and improve component parts of a skill and therefore the skill overall.’
...is positive and concentrates only on the good elements of a candidate’s performance.’
...is negative and concentrates only on the poor elements of a candidate’s performance.’
...compares a candidate’s performance with the performance of others.’
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: ...encourages a learner to practice and improve component parts of a skill and therefore the skill overall.’

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following statements is the most accurate in relation to the potential for assessment to encourage learning?
options: All assessment can encourage learning when appropriate feedback is given.
Only candidates that are successful are motivated by assessment and wish to learn more.
Candidates who are unsuccessful in assessment are always put off any further learning activity.
Only summative assessment can provide motivation for candidates to learn more.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: All assessment can encourage learning when appropriate feedback is given.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: In relation to assessment, what is meant by the term ‘fairness’?
options: Fairness means that all candidates are given an equal opportunity to succeed.
Fairness means that the assessment is fairly easy.
Fairness means that all candidates will be given a second chance at the assessment.
Fairness is an alternative term which means that the assessment is reliable.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Fairness means that all candidates are given an equal opportunity to succeed.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following statements is the most accurate in relation to assessment of competence?
options: Since competence usually involves a combination of skills, then more than one assessment method will normally be required to test whether or not a candidate is competent.
As long as a candidate can complete a task of work then they are competent regardless of how they do it.
Competence can only be assessed by direct observation of a candidate carrying out a physical task.
The best method to use for testing a candidate’s competence is always a combination of written and oral tests.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Since competence usually involves a combination of skills, then more than one assessment method will normally be required to test whether or not a candidate is competent.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the given statements is the most accurate in relation to the learning objectives used in a programme of learning?
options: A learning objective is a specific statement which describes what the learner should be able to do, or will know, after completing a section within a programme of learning.
A learning objective is a specific statement which describes what the learner should be able to do, or will know, after completing a programme of learning.
A learning objective is a specific statement which describes what the teacher or trainer will do in order that the learner will learn something during a programme of learning.
A learning objective is a general statement which describes what the learner should be able to do, or will know, after completing a programme of learning.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: A learning objective is a specific statement which describes what the learner should be able to do, or will know, after completing a section within a programme of learning.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Select from the options given the one that best describes the main characteristics of a learning objective.
options: It should be specific and measurable.
It should be short and measurable.
It should be specific and short.
It should be general and measurable.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: It should be specific and measurable.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following statements is the most accurate in relation to a person who is given a completely new work role?
options: There may be a need to give additional training to the person in order to improve their existing skills or teach them additional skills
If a person has been competent in their former work role then they will be competent in any new role.
Training is expensive, so it should only be given when new technology is introduced in the work place.
The only way to learn how to perform a new work role is ‘on the job’ so providing additional training is a waste of time and effort
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: There may be a need to give additional training to the person in order to improve their existing skills or teach them additional skills

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following best describes a performance improvement plan that is drawn up following an assessment?
options: It is a plan agreed between the assessor and candidate following feedback to improve candidate performance in areas of weakness.
It is a plan drawn up by the assessor to improve candidate performance in areas of weakness.
It is a plan drawn up by the candidate to improve their performance in areas of weakness.
It is a plan drawn up by the assessor to improve the format of the assessment and the way it was carried out.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: It is a plan agreed between the assessor and candidate following feedback to improve candidate performance in areas of weakness.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: How can oral questioning be used to confirm a candidate’s competence following an assessment by direct observation in which they have performed a practical task?
options: Answering oral questions allows the candidate to provide evidence of their knowledge, understanding and other skills required to confirm competence
Oral questions allow the candidate to verbally report on how they performed the task which is all that is required to demonstrate competence.
Oral questioning gives the candidate the opportunity to say what they did wrong during the observational assessment and that is sufficient for the assessor to judge them competent.
Correctly answering oral questions is sufficient evidence of competence on its own, so it is the best method for an assessor to use if they didn’t observe the candidate throughout the task.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Answering oral questions allows the candidate to provide evidence of their knowledge, understanding and other skills required to confirm competence

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: In relation to assessment by direct observation, why is it important that the assessor clearly defines the required performance criteria?
options: The performance criteria define exactly what the candidate should be assessed against.
The performance criteria will provide the candidate with a step by step guide on how to perform an assigned task.
The performance criteria act as a guide for the assessor if he is unfamiliar with the assessment task.
The performance criteria are important, as they are used solely to set a time limit on an assessment.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: The performance criteria define exactly what the candidate should be assessed against.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following statements is most accurate in relation to an assessor’s preparation for assessment of a candidate by direct observation?
options: It is essential that an assessor should define the learning objectives and performance criteria as an initial part of their preparation for the assessment.
As long as the assessor has selected some task for the candidate to perform their preparation is complete.
The assessor should ensure that the candidate is aware of the venue and time for the assessment; any other information can be given when the assessment takes place.
The assessor doesn’t need to check that the assessment venue is properly prepared; this is usually the candidate’s responsibility.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: It is essential that an assessor should define the learning objectives and performance criteria as an initial part of their preparation for the assessment.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Oral questioning can be used by an assessor to fully assess a candidate’s affective skills.’ Is this statement accurate?
options: No, although oral questioning can be used to partly assess these skills, it is necessary to combine this method with observation of behaviour to fully assess affective skills.
Yes, this is the most common method of assessment used to fully assess affective skills.
Yes, using oral questions is a much better method to use than any other method, particularly direct observation.
No, oral questioning cannot usually be used to assess any part of a candidate’s affective skills.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: No, although oral questioning can be used to partly assess these skills, it is necessary to combine this method with observation of behaviour to fully assess affective skills.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which of the following statements is the most accurate in relation to assessment by direct observation?
options: It can normally be used alone to assess a candidate’s proficiency in a physical activity, but not always their competence.
It cannot normally be used alone to assess a candidate’s proficiency in a physical activity or their competence.
It can normally be used alone to fully assess both a candidate’s proficiency in a physical activity and their competence.
It can normally be used alone to assess a candidate’s proficiency in a physical activity and their knowledge and understanding.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: It can normally be used alone to assess a candidate’s proficiency in a physical activity, but not always their competence.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following statements is the most accurate in relation to the limitations of using oral questioning when assessing a candidate?
options: Oral questioning does not allow an assessor to make a proper judgement of the candidate’s psychomotor skills.
Oral questioning does not allow an assessor to make a proper judgement of the candidate’s knowledge and understanding.
Oral questioning, combined with an assessment by direct observation, cannot usually be used to confirm a candidate’s competence.
There are no limitations to the use of oral questioning when assessing any of a candidate’s proficiencies.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Oral questioning does not allow an assessor to make a proper judgement of the candidate’s psychomotor skills.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: In relation to assessing a candidate’s language skills, which one of the following is best suited for assessment by oral questioning?
options: Speaking and listening skills.
Writing and listening skills.
Full competence in a language.
Speaking and writing skills.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Speaking and listening skills.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: In relation to direct observation of a candidate, which one of the following is correct regarding any limitations of using this method of assessment?
options: Some candidates may not perform to their full potential if they feel uncomfortable being observed.
The only limitation to using direct observational methods for assessment is that it is time consuming.
Assessing by direct observation is usually sufficient to fully establish whether or not a candidate is competent.
There are no limitations in using direct observation as a method of assessment.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Some candidates may not perform to their full potential if they feel uncomfortable being observed.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: In relation to the assessment of seafarers, which one of the following can written assignments and projects be best used to provide?
options: Evidence to support entries in a work record book.
Evidence of psychomotor skills ability
Evidence of affective skills ability
Full evidence of competence in practical activities
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Evidence to support entries in a work record book.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following statements is most accurate in relation to the use of oral questions for group assessment?
options: Some candidates may be more comfortable in a group situation and this may encourage them to contribute more.
It is the best form of assessment, as someone in the group is sure to know the correct answer and so the group will pass the assessment
It is a good method to adopt, as the weak candidates will probably gain all of the necessary knowledge from the strong candidates.
It is easy for an assessor to identify a candidate who is not contributing and directly question them to show how weak they are.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Some candidates may be more comfortable in a group situation and this may encourage them to contribute more.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Are there any advantages in using oral questioning when assessing a candidate on a one to one basis?
options: Yes, follow-up questions can be adjusted to the candidate’s response and therefore allow assessment of different cognitive and affective skills.
The only real advantage is that the assessor can see for themselves if the candidate knows anything related to the subject.
No, there are no real advantages; the assessor would always be better using written questions to assess in a one to one situation.
Yes, this is the best method of assessment for the assessor to use in a one on one situation, no matter what skills are being assessed.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Yes, follow-up questions can be adjusted to the candidate’s response and therefore allow assessment of different cognitive and affective skills.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: In relation to the assessment of seafarers, which of the following can be easily assessed using multiple choice type questions?
options: Knowledge and understanding.
Psychomotor skills.
The higher cognitive skills and affective skills.
Competence.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Knowledge and understanding.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following is the main limitation of using oral questioning for a group assessment?
options: It is difficult for the assessor to be sure that all candidates have all of the required knowledge.
It is difficult for the assessor to think of sufficient questions to ask.
The assessor will not be able to remember all of the individuals in the group.
The assessor will not be able to hear the answer if everyone in the group is answering at the same time.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: It is difficult for the assessor to be sure that all candidates have all of the required knowledge.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following is the use of 'open book' tests best suited for assessing?
options: Some of the higher order cognitive skills.
Knowledge
Affective skills
Psychomotor skills
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Some of the higher order cognitive skills.

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which one of the following is 'assessment by direct observation' the best method of assessment for an assessor to use?
options: Psychomotor skills
Competence
Knowledge
Cognitive skills
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: Psychomotor skills

CD0263 — Principles of assessment.question: Which of the following statements is the most accurate in relation to using oral questioning in a group assessment situation?
options: The assessor will need to identify the less proactive group members and give them the opportunity to demonstrate their knowledge, usually by asking direct questions.
In a group assessment situation the more proactive candidates always encourage the less proactive candidates to involve themselves.
If individual candidates within a group do not voluntarily contribute answers the assessor should just fail them.
As long as some members of the group answer each of the questions asked by an assessor the assessor should award the whole group a pass mark.
CD0263 — Principles of assessment.answer: The assessor will need to identify the less proactive group members and give them the opportunity to demonstrate their knowledge, usually by asking direct questions.

CD0264 — Onboard assessment.question: Which one of the given options is the main reason why the use of leading questions should be avoided by an assessor when testing candidates using oral questions?
options: Leading questions usually contain at least part of the answer that is required or an obvious clue to the answer and therefore they do not effectively test the candidate.
Leading questions tend to unsettle candidates which may affect their performance.
Leading questions are only suitable for confirming a candidate’s competence and do not test their cognitive skills.
The language required for leading questions is too complicated and this will only confuse the candidate.
CD0264 — Onboard assessment.answer: Leading questions usually contain at least part of the answer that is required or an obvious clue to the answer and therefore they do not effectively test the candidate.

CD0264 — Onboard assessment.question: Which one of the statements given in the options describes one of the main responsibilities of a candidate for assessment by direct observation?
options: They must familiarise themselves with all details of the assessment provided by the assessor before the assessment.
They must complete the assessment in the shortest time possible.
They must ensure the assessment venue is properly prepared for the assessment.
They must ensure that the assessment decision is properly recorded in a secure record system.
CD0264 — Onboard assessment.answer: They must familiarise themselves with all details of the assessment provided by the assessor before the assessment.

CD0264 — Onboard assessment.question: Which one of the statements given in the options is the best description of the term ‘performance criteria’ in relation to assessment in competency based programme of learning?
options: They are clear statements which describe the level and quality of performance that a candidate must meet in order to demonstrate competence.
They are general statements which describe the competence that is being assessed.
They are clear statements which define the time that is allowed for an assessment task.
They are general statements which describe the performance that a candidate must demonstrate.
CD0264 — Onboard assessment.answer: They are clear statements which describe the level and quality of performance that a candidate must meet in order to demonstrate competence.

CD0264 — Onboard assessment.question: In relation to the use of divergent questions during oral assessment, which one of the statements given in the options is the most accurate?
options: This type of question is best used to test the higher cognitive skills as the candidate will need to evaluate and analyse the possible answers in order to decide on the most appropriate.
This type of question is best used to test knowledge as the candidate will need to recall the correct answer from memory.
This type of question is best used to test the higher cognitive skills as the candidate will need to remember the correct answer.
This type of question is best used to test the range of psychomotor skills associated with a particular competence.
CD0264 — Onboard assessment.answer: This type of question is best used to test the higher cognitive skills as the candidate will need to evaluate and analyse the possible answers in order to decide on the most appropriate.

CD0264 — Onboard assessment.question: Select from the given options the main reason why it is important to limit the expected duration of an assessment during the planning stage?
